short_comment: Gordon recorded five tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday's 30-24 win over the Patriots.
long_comment: Gordon's sack came early -- he brought down Drake Maye for a loss of one yard on a fourth-down play during the Patriots' first offensive drive. The star cornerback has been a terror for opposing offenses through his first two games, as he's already blown by his previous career high with 4.0 sacks. Gordon has done that despite playing a modest 48 defensive snaps across the two contests. He upped his snap share to 58 percent Thursday (after posting a 31 percent mark in his season debut Week 6) and should continue to increase his time on the field as he moves further past a calf injury.

short_comment: Thieneman tallied eight tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, in a 30-24 victory versus the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: Thieneman's eight stops led the Bears. The rookie safety also got to the quarterback for a second straight game, as he was credited with a half-sack of Drake Maye in the fourth quarter. Thieneman has already established himself as a viable IDP asset, posting at least six tackles in six of seven contests and recording 1.5 sacks along with an interception through seven games.

short_comment: Jackson finished with six tackles (three solo) and an interception Thursday in a 30-24 victory over New England.
long_comment: Jackson's six stops were good for second-most on Chicago. However, his biggest impact came on a second-quarter interception of Drake Maye in the Bears' end zone to snuff out what looked to be a Patriots scoring drive. Jackson played every Chicago defensive snap Thursday and has posted a snap share of over 79 percent each of the past three weeks after logging less than half of the team's defensive snaps Weeks 1-4.

short_comment: Roush is expected to get more work on offense after Cole Kmet (knee) landed on injured reserve Friday.
long_comment: Roush didn't catch a pass against New England on Thursday, marking his third straight game without a reception. However, he's currently the only healthy tight end on the Bears' roster aside from starter Colston Loveland, so Roush figures to be in line for an expanded role moving forward. With that said, Loveland has logged 57 or more receiving yards and six or more catches three of the past four weeks and is clearly the Bears' go-to tight end in the passing game, so Roush's anticipated increase of offensive snaps doesn't necessarily make him a viable option in fantasy.

short_comment: Raymond did not catch either of his two targets and returned one punt for seven yards Thursday in a 30-24 win over New England.
long_comment: Raymond started at WR for Chicago and got plenty of playing time, logging 48 of 69 snaps on offense. However, he was unable to make an impact, finishing without a catch for the first time this season. Top wideouts Luther Burden and Rome Odunze combined for eight catches, 199 yards and a touchdown Thursday, and Raymond figures to compete for scraps whenever that pair is healthy.

short_comment: Johnson rushed twice for 13 yards in the Bears' 30-24 victory over the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: Johnson played just 10 offensive snaps to D'Andre Swift's 54 in the contest. The running back did not see much action as he filled in for the injured Kyle Monangai (toe) as a rotational option for the Bears' offense. Johnson also saw one snap with the special teams unit.

short_comment: The NFL reinstated Sweat on Friday after he served a two-game suspension for violating the league's performance-enhancing substances policy.
long_comment: The defensive end is set to return to practice in Week 8 and should play in the team's Monday Night Football showdown against the Seahawks. Sweat has logged seven tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his five regular-season appearances so far in 2026.

short_comment: The Bears placed Kmet (knee) on injured reserve Friday.
long_comment: Kmet suffered a season-ending right knee injury during the fourth quarter of the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday. Even with the emergence of Colston Loveland, Kmet was still a key piece in Chicago's offense as a run blocker, and he'll end his 2026 regular season with a 10-87-1 receiving line (on 14 targets) across seven games. Rookie third-rounder Sam Roush is the only other healthy tight end on the 53-man roster other than Loveland, so the Bears could look to bolster the position group by trade or free agency.

short_comment: Odunze brought in four of five targets for 69 yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: Odunze was encouragingly efficient in the high-scoring win, but he once again saw fellow wideout Luther Burden be more productive. Burden's 130 receiving yards led the Bears on the night, and Odunze appears to have fallen into more of a de facto No. 2 role at this point in the season. Odunze still carries solid fantasy value, however, and he'll carry a 24-381-0 line on 38 targets into a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

short_comment: Loveland secured seven of 12 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown during the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: The second-year tight end continued to shake out of his early-season slump, putting together his second fantasy-friendly performance in a five-day span. Loveland led the Bears in receptions and targets on the night with figures that also qualified as season highs, and he added his second touchdown in five days on a 12-yard grab early in the third quarter. He has a 13-134-2 line in the last two games alone and should continue playing a key role in a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2, and he could be in line for even heavier involvement if Cole Kmet (knee) is unable to suit up.

short_comment: Santos went 3-for-4 on field-goal tries and made all three of his extra-point attempts in Thursday's 30-24 win over New England.
long_comment: Santos put the first points on the board with a 43-yard field goal in the first quarter and added a 31-yarder in the second. He had a chance to give Chicago a two-score lead midway through the fourth quarter but clanged a 53-yard attempt off the right upright. However, Santos atoned for that miss in dramatic fashion, knocking in a 58-yard field goal -- the longest make of his career -- with less than two minutes remaining to essentially seal the win for the Bears. He's now 11-for-15 on field-goal tries this season, including 3-for-5 from 50-plus yards.

short_comment: Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 12 yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: With Kyle Monangai (toe/thumb) out for a third straight game, Swift once again handled a workhorse role and parlayed it into some solid production. Swift's rushing yardage total was his third highest of the season, and the veteran back got into the end zone for the third straight game on a four-yard run late in the first quarter. He's up to seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but his touches will take a hit if Monangai is able to get healthy enough over the extended time between Thursday's game and a Week 8 road matchup against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2 to suit up for that contest.

short_comment: Burden brought in all four targets for 130 yards and a touchdown and rushed once for seven yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: Burden comfortably led the Bears in receiving yards with the second-highest total of his career, and he added his second touchdown catch of the season on a 24-yard grab just before halftime. He also had a game-long 58-yard catch late in the first quarter to set up a D'Andre Swift four-yard touchdown one play later, and the fleet-footed receiver has accumulated 225 of his 491 receiving yards on the season in the last two games alone. Burden has arguably overtaken Rome Odunze as Chicago's most explosive pass-catching weapon, and he should play a critical role again in a Week 8 road showdown against the Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

short_comment: Williams completed 22 of 33 passes for 308 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing five times for 18 yards in the Bears' 30-24 win over the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: Williams spearheaded another prolific performance for the Bears offense, leading his squad to another 30-point tally while eclipsing the 300-yard mark for the second time in five days. He tied his season high with 9.3 yards per attempt, and he accomplished his stellar numbers while focusing on a tight pool of five targets. The 2024 first overall pick's two touchdown passes went to Luther Burden (24 yards) and Colston Loveland (12 yards), marking Williams' first multi-TD tally since Week 1. Williams appears to be clicking on all cylinders in his second season in head coach Ben Johnson's aggressive offense, now having completed 71.0 percent of his passes for 1,020 yards through four games heading into a Week 8 road showdown with the defending champion Seahawks on Monday night, Nov. 2.

short_comment: Muhammad (toe) is doubtful to return to Thursday night's contest against the Patriots.
long_comment: Muhammad is dealing with a toe injury, and he will now likely be forced to watch the remainder of the game from the Bears' sideline. In Muhammad's absence, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips are both candidates to see an increase in workload at cornerback.

short_comment: Stevenson (hip) is active for Thursday night's contest against New England.
long_comment: Stevenson will make his return to action after missing the team's Week 6 win over Atlanta while nursing a hip injury that he suffered a week prior versus Green Bay. The 26-year-old will be back in his starting role at cornerback, and his primary task Thursday night may be slowing down A.J. Brown.

short_comment: Jackson (hip/quadricep) does not have any injury designation ahead of Thursday night's game against the Patriots.
long_comment: Jackson picked up multiple injuries in the Bears' Week 6 win over the Falcons. The offensive guard was able to upgrade his practice participation in every session during the team's short turnaround ahead of Thursday Night Football and is all set to suit up for the contest against the Patriots.

short_comment: Carter recorded nine tackles (three solo) and a pass defense during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
long_comment: Carter didn't play every defensive snap for just the first time this season, but his nine stops were tied with Bryan Cook for most on the Bengals. Carter has logged at least five stops in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 50 tackles (22 solo), including 1.5 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble in 2026.

short_comment: Mafe finished Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens with five tackles (three solo), including 1.5 sacks.
long_comment: Mafe got to Tyler Huntley for a six-yard sack midway through the first quarter before splitting another sack with Bryan Cook in the fourth. Mafe has logged at least 1.0 sacks in three consecutive games and is up to 4.5 sacks through six regular-season games, which already surpasses his total from 2025 with Seattle (2.0 sacks across 17 regular-season contests).

short_comment: Cook recorded nine tackles (six solo), including 0.5 sacks, during the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
long_comment: Cook and Boye Mafe combined for a split sack on Tyler Huntley midway through the fourth quarter, which was Cook's first sack since his rookie year in 2022. The fifth-year safety is up to 26 tackles (18 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through five regular-season games.

short_comment: Knight totaled eight tackles (two solo) and an interception during the Bengals' win over the Ravens on Sunday.
long_comment: Knight finished third on the team in tackles behind Bryan Cook and Barrett Carter during the victory, in addition to snagging his first interception of the campaign. The 26-year-old continues to have a productive season, as he's now recorded seven or more tackles in five of his six appearances, bringing his total on the campaign to 50 (21 solo).

short_comment: The Bengals placed All (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: Though All will be eligible to return from IR as soon as Week 12, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relays that the third-year tight end is feared to have sustained a season-ending ACL tear of his right knee during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens. All will likely undergo further testing over the next day or two before the Bengals provide an updated diagnosis, but if the ACL tear is confirmed, the 26-year-old could be sidelined into the 2027 season. He previously tore the ACL in the same knee in 2023 during his final collegiate season at Iowa and during his 2024 rookie campaign with Cincinnati.

short_comment: Meyers failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
long_comment: With Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both fully healthy, Meyers played just 20 of 53 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on Joe Burrow's 32 dropbacks. Outside of his 7-82-0 receiving performance in Week 4 against the Jaguars, Meyers has totaled six catches for 59 yards in the other five games.

short_comment: Dugger (quadriceps) won't play in Sunday's game against the Titans, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Dugger was injured in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens and did not return. The 30-year-old will now miss at least one game, and while there will likely be more updates on his health moving forward, he should be considered week-to-week. Dugger hasn't seen consistent action on the defensive side of the ball, though his absence will be felt on special teams.

short_comment: The Bengals signed Grandy off the Vikings' practice squad Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: Grandy spent the previous two seasons with Cincinnati prior to being a part of final cuts this past summer. With Tanner Hudson (pectoral) done for the season and Erick All going down with a knee injury Sunday against the Ravens, Grandy gives the Bengals another reliable tight end behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample.

short_comment: Chase brought in five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
long_comment: Chase played a clear second fiddle to Tee Higgins, who had a team-high 148 receiving yards, as the former finished second to his teammate in receptions and receiving yards while tying him for the team lead in targets. Chase also recorded a touchdown grab for the second straight game, bringing in a two-yard scoring strike from Joe Burrow at the halfway point of the fourth quarter. Chase is still in search of his first 100-yard game of the season, and he'll look to break the ice on that front in a Week 8 home matchup against a vulnerable Titans secondary next Sunday.

short_comment: Gesicki caught his only target for a six-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
long_comment: Gesicki isn't seeing reliable volume in the form of targets, but he's been a big factor in the red zone this season, as he now has five touchdowns in six games. He's already one away from matching his career high, which was set in 2020 with the Dolphins. Gesicki is repping as the Bengals' slot receiver between Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, but the latter two dominate the passing looks from Joe Burrow.

short_comment: Perine rushed four times for 16 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
long_comment: The running back wasn't targeted in the passing game, but Perine notably subbed in for Chase Brown at the goal line to punch in a one-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter. It's become apparent that the coaches are trusting Perine more, and it's having an effect on Brown's production. Perine is up to 31 carries for 126 yards (4.1 YPC) and one touchdown through six games this season.

short_comment: Sample caught both of his targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.
long_comment: Sample entered Week 7 with just five catches for 24 yards on six targets across five games, so he doubled his yardage total and secured his first touchdown with Sunday's performance. It goes without saying, but Sample isn't on the fantasy football radar.

short_comment: Brown rushed 11 times for 39 yards and brought in four of five targets for 19 yards in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
long_comment: Brown didn't partake in the Bengals' five-touchdown second-half explosion, but the versatile back had a serviceable day on a per-touch basis. However, Brown hasn't really come close to reaching the 100-yard mark on the ground in any game this season -- the closest he's come is 80 yards -- and he's been at 61 yards or fewer in five of six contests. Brown's pass-catching work continues to typically be plentiful, but he still has a relatively modest outlook heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

short_comment: McPherson did not attempt a field goal and made all five of his PATs in Sunday's 35-13 win over Baltimore.
long_comment: McPherson and the rest of the Bengals were blanked before halftime, but the kicker was able to finish off five touchdown drives in the second half. McPherson has now attempted one or zero field goals in three straight games after opening the season with multiple field-goal makes in each of the team's first three contests.

short_comment: Burrow completed 22 of 30 passes for 292 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 12 yards in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
long_comment: Burrow couldn't lead the Bengals to a single point in the first half, but the 2020 first overall pick came out of intermission locked in. He helped spearhead five consecutive scoring drives to start the second half, capping four of them with touchdown passes to Mike Gesicki (six yards), Tee Higgins (13 yards), Ja'Marr Chase (two yards ) and Drew Sample (16 yards). The game marked Burrow's second straight with four scoring tosses and zero interceptions, and both his passing yardage total and 73.3 percent completion rate were his second highest of the season. He'll take 1,653 passing yards and a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

short_comment: Higgins secured six of seven targets for 148 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
long_comment: The Bengals' air attack as a whole got off to a very sluggish start, leading to a scoreless first half. However, Cincinnati exploded for 35 points after intermission, and Higgins played a big role by posting team-high reception and receiving yardage totals while tying for the team lead in targets. The veteran wideout also recorded his second touchdown catch of the campaign on a 13-yard grab with just under five minutes remaining in the third quarter that gave Cincinnati a 14-13 lead. Higgins is averaging an outstanding 17.3 yards per reception on a 33-571-2 receiving line heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

short_comment: Young (knee) was not listed on the Bengals' injury report Wednesday.
long_comment: Young missed each of the Bengals' two games prior to the Week 6 bye due to a knee injury. The extra rest has paid dividends for the rookie fourth-rounder, who is on track to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown against the Ravens. He's operated in a minimal role offensively this season, having logged only two catches on as many targets for nine yards across three games.

short_comment: Hudson (pectoral) was placed on injured reserve by the Bengals on Monday.
long_comment: Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle during the team's 31-24 win over Miami in Week 5, so his transition to IR comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All will continue to operate as the team's primary options at tight end.

short_comment: The Bengals placed Bozeman on injured reserve Monday due to a fractured forearm, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The third-year linebacker out of Southern Miss sustained the injury during Sunday's 31-24 win over the Dolphins, and he'll now be sidelined for at least four weeks after landing on IR. Bozeman had suited up in four of the Bengals' first five contests of the season, seeing most of his action on special teams while tallying four tackles.

short_comment: Schwesinger finished Sundays' 27-24 win over the Titans with eight tackles (four solo).
long_comment: Schwesinger finished third on the Browns in tackles Sunday behind both Quincy Williams and Ronnie Hickman (10 each). Schwesinger has played every single defensive snap through seven regular-season games and has logged at least eight stops in six of those contests. He's up to 64 total tackles on the year, which leads the Browns and is sixth-most in the NFL.

short_comment: Hickman registered 10 tackles (six solo) and a fumble recovery during Sundays' 27-24 win over Tennessee.
long_comment: Hickman and Quincy Williams co-led the Browns in tackles Sunday, with the former playing every defensive snap for the sixth time this season. Hickman's 10 tackles were his most of the season, and the fourth-year safety is up to 41 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and two fumble recoveries through seven regular-season contests.

short_comment: Williams finished Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans with 10 tackles (seven solo).
long_comment: Williams was working through neck and back injuries during Week 7 prep, but he was cleared to play Sunday and ended up playing every single defensive snap while co-leading the Browns in tackles with Ronnie Hickman. It was the second time in three games that Williams recorded double-digit stops, and he is up to 50 tackles (30 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses and three forced fumbles through seven regular-season contests.

short_comment: Davis (quadriceps) will spend the rest of the 2026 season on injured reserve after his 21-day practice window expired Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: Davis injured his quad during training camp in late July and started the regular season on IR. His 21-day window opened Oct. 6, but he has not progressed enough in his recovery to warrant his removal from IR. That means that the 2022 sixth-rounder will be sidelined for the rest of the season unless he reaches an injury settlement with the Browns.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: McLaughlin turned five kickoff returns into 117 yards during the Browns' 27-24 win over the Titans on Sunday.
long_comment: McLaughlin played a key role in the Browns' Week 6 win over the Ravens, when he had nine carries for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all four of his targets for 13 yards. However, his role on offense evaporated Sunday due to the returns of both Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. McLaughlin figures to be limited to return duties moving forward unless one or both of Judkins or Sampson misses time.

short_comment: Jeudy caught all four of his targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win at Tennessee.
long_comment: Jeudy now has four catches in each of his last two games, an encouraging sign after he had no more than three in any of the first five games of the season. He's still trailing rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in terms of playing time, however. Jeudy is not on the radar in most formats going into a Week 8 matchup at Pittsburgh.

short_comment: The Browns activated Gabriel (back) from injured reserve Monday.
long_comment: Cleveland needed to make a decision on the quarterback after opening his 21-day practice window 20 days ago, so he'll now join the 53-man roster as one of the team's four quarterbacks. The Browns figure to make a move at the position in the near future, and perhaps they'll try to gauge trade interest in Gabriel.

short_comment: Boston caught three of eight targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The wide receiver was the favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year after the first five weeks of the season, but he's now posted back-to-back subpar games against the Ravens and Titans. During those two contests, Boston has four catches for 42 yards on 13 targets. He's been extremely inefficient with his looks and isn't getting loose for big plays over the top of the defense. He'll try to get back on track next Sunday in Pittsburgh.

short_comment: Fannin caught six of nine targets for 91 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The second-year tight end delivered a season high in receiving yards, and Fannin's last catch was his biggest. With the game tied at 24-24 in the final minute of the fourth quarter, Fannin took a short pass over the middle from Deshaun Watson and tacked on about 30 yards after the catch to set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. Fannin will take a 25-257-3 line on 39 targets through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Steelers.

short_comment: Sampson carried the ball six times for 45 yards and caught all three of his targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
long_comment: Seeing his first action since Week 1, and his first offensive snaps of the season, after recovering from a knee injury, Sampson logged nine touches to Quinshon Judkins' 18 in impressive performances from both. Sampson is the clear No. 2 RB when the Browns' backfield is at 100 percent, but there could be enough volume for Sampson to have fantasy value in that role given the team's fairly underpowered aerial attack. Sampson will look to stay productive in Week 8 against the Steelers.

short_comment: Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards with an interception in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans. He added 19 yards and a touchdown on three carries.
long_comment: While he didn't throw a TD pass for a second straight game, Watson produced a season high in passing yards and scored his first rushing TD since Week 2 of the 2024 season on a nine-yard scamper in the fourth quarter. Watson also led his fifth game-winning, fourth-quarter drive of the year, completing another comeback after the Browns fell behind 14-0 early. The veteran QB will take a 7:3 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 8 meeting with the Steelers.

short_comment: Concepcion caught eight of 10 targets for 129 yards and added 23 yards on three carries in Sunday's 27-24 win over Tennessee.
long_comment: The rookie wideout put together a breakout performance, with his 10 targets, eight catches and 129 receiving yards all being season highs. If fact, the yardage total was more than Concepcion had produced in any two of his first six NFL games combined. Concepcion's chemistry with Deshaun Watson is growing, and he'll be hunting for his first career touchdown in Week 8 against the Steelers.

short_comment: Judkins carried the ball 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans. He also caught his only target for eight yards.
long_comment: Making his return from an ankle injury that sidelined him in Week 6, Judkins put together his best performance of the season, punching in red-zone TDs from five yards out in the first quarter and six yards out in the second. His 96 rushing yards and 104 scrimmage yards were also season highs. Judkins will try to keeping rolling in Week 8 against the Steelers.

short_comment: Szmyt went 2-for-3 on field-goal tries while making all three of his extra-point attempts during Sunday's 27-24 win over Tennessee.
long_comment: Szmyt converted exactly two field goals for the fifth straight week, while Sunday's performance marked his sixth in a row with multiple field-goal makes. The kicker made a 28-yarder as time expired in the first half before hitting the right upright on a 43-yard miss with 14:09 left in the fourth quarter. Szmyt got his redemption later, though, nailing a game-winning 32-yard try in the final seconds of the game. The 28-year-old has now gone 14-for-16 on field-goal tries while making 11 of 12 PATs over the first seven contests during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Howard is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans.
long_comment: Howard was taken to the locker room in the second half and is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. Dawand Jones has taken over at right tackle in Howard's absence.

short_comment: Harden (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Harden tweaked his hamstring in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. Mekhi Blackmon will see more defensive snaps for as long as Harden is out of the game.

short_comment: Sanders is active as the Browns' backup quarterback for Sunday's game against the Titans.
long_comment: After Deshaun Watson had a listless performance in a blowout loss to the Jaguars in Week 1, Ian Rapoport of ESPN had reported that Sanders could get a chance to start as soon as Week 3 if the Browns continued to languish. Watson has since steadied the ship, leading the Browns to wins in four of their last five games to put them atop the AFC North standings heading into Week 7 action. As a result, Sanders doesn't appear likely to threaten Watson's standing atop the depth chart anytime soon, though Sanders will continue to suit up on game days ahead of rookie Taylen Green, who will once again be inactive Sunday as the Browns' emergency No. 3 quarterback.

short_comment: Ward (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Titans.
long_comment: Ward popped up on Friday's injury report due to a hand injury, logging a limited session in the process. A late addition to the injury report isn't typically a good sign, but the veteran cornerback has been given the green light to play in Sunday's road game. Ward has 25 tackles (15 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and two forced fumbles through six regular-season games.

short_comment: Collins and the Browns agreed to a two-year, $30 million contract extension Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: The deal includes $23 million in guaranteed money and keeps Collins in Cleveland through the 2028 season. The veteran defensive tackle has accumulated 3.5 sacks over his last three games and has operated in a key role on the Browns' defensive line alongside Mason Graham, Isaiah McGuire and Jared Verse.

short_comment: Overshown posted six tackles (five solo) and two pass defenses (including one interception) during the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday.
long_comment: Overshown was given the green light by medical staff to play Monday after missing the Cowboys' five previous games due to a hamstring injury. The fourth-year linebacker ended up co-leading Dallas in tackles and he picked off Tanner McKee midway through the fourth quarter. Overshown has played in only 21 regular-season games since being selected by the Cowboys in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft, but he's still a key piece in the defense when healthy.

short_comment: Downs recorded five tackles (three solo) during the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday.
long_comment: Downs was on the field for 56 of the Cowboys' 58 defensive snaps, which broke his streak of playing every snap at five consecutive games. The rookie first-rounder leads the Cowboys with 48 total tackles through seven regular-season games, which is also fifth-most in the NFL among rookies.

short_comment: Ferguson failed to haul in his lone target during Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
long_comment: Monday was the first time since Week 8 of the 2025 season that Ferguson failed to record a catch, and the only pass he saw from Dak Prescott was on a broken play in the red zone early in the fourth quarter. Ferguson's 38 offensive snaps were only two more than fellow tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford, and the latter's role in the offense has grown over the last few weeks at the expense of the former. Week 8 against the Cardinals presents itself as a bounce-back opportunity for Ferguson, seeing as Arizona's defense ranks 27th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to tight ends.

short_comment: Goodson turned 10 carries into 38 yards and returned two kickoffs for 42 yards during the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday.
long_comment: The Cowboys relied heavily on the run game Monday, and Goodson saw a season-high 10 rushes as a result, although that was still well behind the workload of lead back Javonte Williams, who turned 25 carries into a career-high 155 yards and a score. Goodson nearly found the end zone himself after returning a 91-yard kickoff to the house in the second quarter, only for the touchdown to be nullified by a holding penalty on Dallas. He's limited to RB2 duties for the time being but would step into an elevated role if Williams were to ever miss time. The Cowboys will head back home for Week 8 against the Cardinals, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (126.4).

short_comment: Schoonmaker went without a target while playing 11 of the Cowboys' 68 offensive snaps in Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
long_comment: After drawing even with Brevyn Spann-Ford in snaps during the Cowboys' Week 1 loss to the Giants, Schoonmaker has settled in as the clear No. 3 option on the depth chart at tight end behind Jake Ferguson and Spann-Ford in the subsequent six games. He's played less than 20 percent of the offensive snaps in four consecutive contests, drawing just one target during that span while functioning mainly as a blocker during his time on the field.

short_comment: Spann-Ford finished with two catches for 11 yards on two targets in Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
long_comment: With the Cowboys opening the game in 12 personnel, Spann-Ford was credited with a start and was on the field for 36 of the team's 68 offensive snaps on the night (52.9 percent). Though Jake Ferguson is locked in as Dallas' top tight end, Spann-Ford has consistently repped ahead of Luke Schoonmaker as the No. 2 option at the position since Week 2. While he's mainly functioned as a blocker, Spann-Ford has been a solid complementary option in the passing game with a 9-79-0 line on 13 targets.

short_comment: Flournoy secured all four targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
long_comment: Flournoy tied with George Pickens for second in receptions and outgained his teammate by 13 receiving yards to finish as the runner-up in that category as well. The second-year wideout has popped for 90- and 70-yard tallies in two of his last three games, and although his week-to-week production remains somewhat erratic, Flournoy does have some upside thanks to his growing chemistry with Dak Prescott.

short_comment: Pickens brought in four of six targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
long_comment: Pickens tied for second in receptions and finished third in receiving yards on the night for the Cowboys, and the athletic receiver added his second touchdown of the season on a highly difficult catch in the right corner of the end zone with just under six minutes remaining in the second quarter. Both of Pickens' scoring grabs this season have come in the last three games, and he's now boasting a 37-485-2 line on 58 targets as a Week 8 home matchup against the Cardinals approaches this Sunday.

short_comment: Williams rushed 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
long_comment: Williams broke out for a new single-game career high in rushing yards during the impressive victory, sealing the win with a two-yard scoring run just ahead of the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. The remarkable performance also marked Williams' first 100-yard tally of the season, and he's been highly rewarding for fantasy managers by scoring a touchdown in five straight games. Williams should have a prime opportunity to continue building on his strong first half of the season in Week 8, as he'll face a vulnerable Cardinals run defense at home on Sunday.

short_comment: Prescott completed 15 of 27 passes for 212 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for eight yards in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night. He also had a two-point conversion run.
long_comment: The Cowboys were able to keep Prescott upright throughout the night, and the veteran signal-caller leveraged the solid protection into his first multi-touchdown-pass tally since Week 2. Prescott connected with CeeDee Lamb (nine, 16 yards) and George Pickens (21 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and although his 55.6 percent completion rate was a season low, Prescott was able to steer clear of interceptions after throwing two apiece in Weeks 5 and 6. Prescott now has 1,851 passing yards and a 13:5 TD:INT going into a favorable Week 8 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

short_comment: Lamb brought in five of 12 targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
long_comment: Lamb led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he added his fifth and sixth touchdowns of the season on nine- and 16-yard scoring grabs. The veteran star has 70 or more receiving yards in two straight and five of his last six contests overall, and Lamb's average of 11.6 targets per game gives him an elite floor heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

short_comment: Locke (foot) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Monday's game against the Eagles.
long_comment: Locke's 21-day practice window opened Friday, and he was a limited participant in each of the last two practices of Week 7 prep. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a foot injury, but he's not quite ready to be activated from IR. His next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Liufau (forearm) has been downgraded from questionable to out ahead of Monday night's game against the Eagles.
long_comment: Liufau was designated to return from injured reserve Thursday and was a full practice participant Friday and Saturday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag, but the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery from a broken left forearm. Given his ability to practice without restrictions, Liufau has a good chance of being activated from IR for Week 8 against the Cardinals on Nov. 1.

short_comment: Durant (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Monday's game against Philadelphia, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
long_comment: Durant was a full practice participant Friday and Saturday, and that was enough for the fifth-year defensive back to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. His presence gives the Cowboys another contributor on special teams and depth in the secondary behind starting outside cornerbacks Joey Porter and DaRon Bland.

short_comment: Thomas was signed to the Cowboys' active roster Tuesday.
long_comment: Thomas will officially join the active roster with Dallas after being elevated from the practice squad for each of the team's last three contests. The 26-year-old will provide the team with an additional experienced option at safety moving forward.

short_comment: Aubrey did not attempt any field goals but converted his only extra-point try during Sunday's 23-13 loss at Green Bay.
long_comment: In a game where the Cowboys fell into a hole early and turned the ball over three times in opposing territory, Aubrey was mostly a spectator, failing to make at least one field goal in a game for the first time since Week 1 against the Giants. Dallas' offense will have better days than it did Sunday, and one of those could come in Week 7 against a Philadelphia defense that has looked poor at times this season.

short_comment: Waddle aggravated a previous chest injury during last week's 30-16 win over the Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will be determined based on how he fares in practice this week, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: Waddle recorded four receptions for 48 yards on seven targets against Arizona before checking out of the game in the fourth quarter due to the lingering chest issue, which had limited his participation in two practices during Week 7 prep. The wideout's practice activity appears likely to be affected in Week 8, but the Broncos aren't yet counting him out from suiting up against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Jones recorded nine tackles (five solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 30-16 win at Arizona.
long_comment: After another solid performance in Week 7, Jones has now posted eight-plus total tackles in four of his last five games. He's easily on pace for a 100-tackle season, and he's solidly on the IDP radar in most formats going into a Week 8 tilt versus a balanced Chiefs offense.

short_comment: Singleton recorded 19 tackles (12 solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 30-16 win at Arizona.
long_comment: The tackle total was Singleton's best since the 2022 season, and he has now tallied double-digit tackles in four of seven games this season. He's far and away the NFL's leading tackler through seven weeks (87 total), and he's a top-tier IDP option in most formats going into a Week 8 matchup versus the Chiefs.

long_comment: questionable

long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Engram caught one of three targets for two yards during Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Engram played a season-low 23 offensive snaps in the victory, and as a result, he was limited to one or zero catches for the fourth time this season. The tight end hasn't reached the end zone since Week 1, and he'll remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Chiefs.

short_comment: Franklin failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Franklin played 28 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. Despite being on the field for 46 percent of the Broncos' offensive plays, the No. 3 option was targeted only twice and failed to catch either pass.

short_comment: Mims caught both of his targets for 53 yards, rushed once for three yards and accumulated 103 yards over four punt returns in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Mims played 16 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The speedy wide receiver was in on just 26 percent of the team's offensive snaps and mainly utilized as a pressure-release option underneath for the Broncos' offense in the win.

short_comment: Sutton caught three of five targets for 45 yards during Sunday's 30-16 win over Arizona.
long_comment: Sutton was able to reel in three passes for the first time since Week 3, and his 45 receiving yards were his second highest total in a contest this year. The wide receiver has had an overall disappointing campaign so far, but Jaylen Waddle (chest) exited the contest in the fourth quarter, so Sutton could be thrust into a more prominent role in Week 8 against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Coleman (ankle) rushed nine times for 54 yards and caught both of his targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Coleman led the team in carries in his return from injured reserve and finished second behind Bo Nix (73) in rushing yards. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey combined for just 29 rushing yards on nine rushing attempts, though Dobbins had a rushing touchdown and Harvey had a receiving touchdown. Coleman was notably the team's running back of choice as the Broncos ran out the clock in the fourth quarter, and head coach Sean Payton said after the game that the team has "got to get (Coleman) more touches," per Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site. Denver will likely continue to utilize all three running backs in Week 8 against the Chiefs, but this was an encouraging performance for Coleman in the rookie fourth-round pick's first action since Week 2.

short_comment: Dobbins rushed six times for 23 yards and a touchdown and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Dobbins extended his touchdown streak to three games with a one-yard rushing score to end the third quarter, but he was far less efficient on the ground than Jonah Coleman, who rushed nine times for 54 yards in his return from an ankle injury, averaging 6.0 YPC to Dobbins' 3.8. Coleman and RJ Harvey each had two catches, with Harvey breaking free for a 52-yard touchdown on one of those receptions, while Dobbins hasn't exceeded 12 receiving yards in a game this season. With Coleman likely to claim a chunk of the rushing opportunities moving forward, Dobbins profiles as a touchdown-dependent Week 8 fantasy option against the Chiefs.

short_comment: Harvey rushed three times for six yards while catching both of his targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Harvey did most of his damage on a 52-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, but he was quiet otherwise. Jonah Coleman turned nine carries and two catches into 69 scrimmage yards in the rookie's return from an ankle injury, while J.K. Dobbins scored a touchdown on one of the latter's six rushing attempts, so Denver has a three-man backfield rotation going ahead of a Week 8 home game against the Chiefs. Harvey has a path to consistent targets as a pass catcher out of the backfield, especially if he continues to capitalize on those opportunities like he did Sunday.

short_comment: Nix completed 15 of 29 passes for 222 yards and a touchdown while rushing seven times for 73 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Nix led the Broncos in rushing yards thanks to a 62-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter, which was the longest regular-season rushing score by a QB since Justin Fields ran in a 67-yard TD in 2022. Nix added a 52-yard touchdown pass to RJ Harvey in the third quarter, but it was another quiet outing as a passer for the third-year QB, as Nix has only one multi-touchdown performance through seven starts and is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Those poor numbers include a 131-yard, one-TD Week 1 performance against the Chiefs, whom the Broncos will host for a Week 8 rematch.

short_comment: Lutz went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 30-16 win over Arizona.
long_comment: Lutz was able to make multiple field goals for the third time in the last four contests. The kicker converted attempts from 48 and 43 yards in the first quarter before later adding a 31-yarder in the fourth quarter. Lutz has now gone 12-for-15 on field-goal attempts while making all 12 of his extra-point tries over the first seven games of the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Allen suffered a hamstring injury in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
long_comment: Allen sustained the injury late in the second half, and more information on the severity will likely be provided in the near future. The defensive lineman's status at the team's first practice of the week Wednesday will shed more light on his availability  moving forward.

short_comment: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
long_comment: Ehlinger will only be available if quarterbacks Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: The Broncos placed Badie (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Per Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette, Badie broke his thumb during the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. Badie is required to miss at least four games, and the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move, and if he's cleared to play Sunday, then he would slot in as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

short_comment: The Broncos placed Elliss (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Elliss was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals due to an ankle injury, which is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. He'll be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. The Broncos will get some pass-rushing reinforcement after Jonathon Cooper was activated from the commissioner's exempt list.

short_comment: Cooper had his roster exemption removed by the Broncos on Saturday and is available for Sunday's road game against the Cardinals, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
long_comment: Cooper opened the season on the commissioner's exempt list while under investigation for domestic incidents that happened in June. Now that he's back on the roster, he could make his 2026 debut Sunday, and his return would bolster a Broncos pass rush that will be without Jonah Elliss (ankle, IR) for at least the next four games. Across 17 regular-season games in 2025, Cooper accumulated 50 tackles (23 solo), including 8.0 sacks, and four pass defenses.

short_comment: Abrams-Draine recorded six tackles (four solo), three pass breakups, including an interception, and one forced fumble in Thursday night's 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks.
long_comment: With Pat Surtain (ankle) inactive for the second straight game, Abrams-Draine played 76.5 percent of the Broncos' defensive snaps and had easily the best game of his young career. He picked off Sam Darnold late in the fourth quarter but was picked on in coverage for much of the night, as the Seahawks avoided Riley Moss' side of the field.

short_comment: McMillian recorded five tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a pair of pass breakups, including an interception, in Thursday night's 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks.
long_comment: With Pat Surtain (ankle) inactive, McMillian saw increased snaps, logging a season-high 76.5 percent of the defensive snaps. His interception of Sam Darnold in overtime set the Broncos up at Seattle's 43-yard line, leading to the eventual game-winning field goal. On the season, McMillian has 16 tackles (12 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and four pass breakups with the one interception.

short_comment: Campbell tallied 11 tackles (eight solo) during the Lions' 20-17 win over the Packers on Sunday.
long_comment: Campbell was on the field for every single defensive snap and led the Lions in tackles. His eight solo stops were a season high, and he's reached double-digit tackles in each of his last three outings. Through six regular-season games, Campbell has 54 tackles (29 solo) and one fumble recovery.

short_comment: Branch recorded four tackles (one solo) and an interception during Sunday's 20-17 win over Green Bay.
long_comment: Branch was given the green light to play Sunday in what was his first game since he tore his Achilles in Week 14 of the 2025 season. He was on the field for 45 of the Lions' 67 defensive snaps (67.2 percent), and his return was highlighted by his interception off of Jordan Love early in the fourth quarter. Having Branch back in the fold significantly boosts the Lions' secondary, especially since the defense ranks dead last in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (291.8). Detroit will stay home for Week 8 to host Minnesota in another NFC North tilt.

short_comment: TeSlaa caught one of his two targets for 10 yards in the Lions' 20-17 win over the Packers on Sunday.
long_comment: TeSlaa played 33 offensive snaps for the Lions in the contest, a 49 percent share of Detroit's offensive plays. However, TeSlaa saw a mere two targets for the second straight game after logging a season-high eight against the Panthers in Week 4, and Sunday's catch was his first since that game as well.

short_comment: Rakestraw (ankle) is not believed to be dealing with a major injury after he was forced to exit Sunday's win over the Packers, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
long_comment: Coach Dan Campbell said Rakestraw could practice this week, and he has a chance to a play Sunday against the undefeated Vikings. Rock Ya-Sin filled in at cornerback following Rakestraw's injury and would be in line for increased snaps on defense if the latter is unable to face Minnesota.

short_comment: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that St. Brown tweaked his ankle during Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers but should be ready to practice Thursday, Richard Silva of The Detroit News reports.
long_comment: Campbell is planning for St. Brown to rest during the Lions' first Week 8 session Wednesday, but the star wideout should be able to practice during the subsequent two days to put himself on a path to play Sunday against the undefeated Vikings. The ankle injury likely explains why he saw a slight decline in playing time -- he logged 53 of 68 offensive snaps (78 percent) -- but St. Brown still  delivered for fantasy managers in the win over Green Bay. Though he was held out of the end zone for the third game in a row, St. Brown finished with nine receptions for a season-high 153 yards.

short_comment: LaPorta caught one of two targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers.
long_comment: It wasn't a happy Tight Ends Day for LaPorta, who had his worst performance of the season despite the fact that Jared Goff threw for over 300 yards. Even with the quiet afternoon, LaPorta still sports a 28-334-3 line on 39 targets through six games, keeping him on pace for a new career high in receiving yards. He faces another tough challenge in Week 8 versus the dominant defense of the undefeated Vikings.

short_comment: Williams caught five of nine targets for 91 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 20-17 win over Green Bay.
long_comment: One game after scoring his first two TDs of the season, Williams struck twice again, hauling in a 16-yard toss from Jared Goff in the first quarter and a 10-yard score in the third. After a slow start to the campaign, Williams has broken out for a 13-240-4 line on 19 targets over the last three contests, and the Lions' Week 6 bye did nothing to cool him off. The fifth-year wideout will carry plenty of momentum into a tough Week 8 matchup against the unbeaten Vikings.

short_comment: Goff completed 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers.
long_comment: It's the third time in six games this season Goff has passed for 300-plus yards, and the fifth time he's tossed multiple TDs. Both of his scores in this one went to Jameson Williams, as he connected with the speedy wideout for a 16-yard strike in the first quarter and a 10-yard touchdown in the third. Goff will take a stellar 14:0 TD:INT into a crucial NFC North battle in Week 8 against the undefeated Vikings.

short_comment: Gibbs carried the ball 29 times for 116 yards and caught five of six targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over Green Bay.
long_comment: For the first time this season, Gibbs failed to get into the end zone, but he made up for it by delivering more than 100 scrimmage yards for the fifth time in six games. The fourth-year back continues to handle a massive workload, averaging 27.7 touches a game, but Gibbs has earned it by leading the NFL in scrimmage TDs with nine and staying neck-and-neck with Bijan Robinson for the lead in scrimmage yards. Gibbs faces his toughest test yet in 2026 against a dominant Vikings defense in Week 8.

short_comment: Bates went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers.
long_comment: Bates was able to convert multiple field-goal attempts for just the second time this season. The kicker split the uprights on a 40-yard try in the second quarter before he sent Green Bay packing with a game-winning 22-yard chip shot as time expired in regulation. Bates has yet to miss a kick this season, going 10-for-10 on field-goal tries, including a 54-yard make in Week 4 against the Panthers, while nailing all 22 of his extra-point attempts over six contests.

short_comment: Mays (wrist) was activated from injured reserve Saturday and no longer has an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: Mays has fully recovered from a fractured wrist that caused him to start the regular season on injured reserve. He should take over for Juice Scruggs as the Lions' starting center for Sunday's NFC North tilt.

short_comment: Ya-Sin (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: The veteran defensive back has been cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury, with Ya-Sin having the benefit of extra rest courtesy of the Week 6 bye. His return gives the Lions depth in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.

short_comment: The Lions signed Carter to the active roster Thursday.
long_comment: Carter last played for Cleveland in 2025, and he served as the team's main return man. The 33-year-old veteran is expected to do the same for Detroit after the season-ending knee injury to Tom Kennedy, per Eric Woodyard of ESPN.com.

short_comment: Lions head coach Dan Campbell stated Kerby (knee) "is in a good headspace" and expects the 25-year-old to play at some point this season, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
long_comment: Joseph has been sidelined for more than a year after sustaining a knee injury in the Week 6 meeting with the Chiefs during the 2025 campaign. While there was hope he would be ready to get back on the field early in the 2026 season, he remains on the reserve/PUP list. With Kerby still out of commission, Chuck Clark is projected to continue handling most of the work at free safety for the foreseeable future.

short_comment: The Lions placed Bartch (foot) on injured reserve Friday.
long_comment: Bartch has already missed three games due to a foot injury that he sustained against the Bills in Week 2. While on IR, he'll be forced to miss at least four games, so Week 11 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 22, is the earliest he can return.

short_comment: The Lions placed White (forearm) on injured reserve Friday.
long_comment: White was diagnosed with a broken forearm following the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. He'll be required to miss at least the next four games on IR, and while he's likely to be sidelined past that minimum window, there's optimism that the veteran linebacker will return at some point this season. Malcolm Rodriguez is the next man up at linebacker in White's absence.

short_comment: The Lions placed Kennedy (knee) on injured reserve Friday.
long_comment: Kennedy suffered a season-ending MCL injury in his right knee during the Lions' Week 5 win over the Cardinals. His move to IR opens a spot on Detroit's 53-man roster, and in his absence, Jacob Saylors is in line to take over return duties on kickoffs and punts.

short_comment: Williams (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: Williams was spotted wearing a walking boot and didn't practice Wednesday. He logged limited practice sessions Thursday and Friday but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation. However, Williams has since been cleared for action after amassing a season-high six total tackles in the 32-26 loss to Carolina in Week 4.

short_comment: Izien recorded 11 tackles (seven solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 32-26 loss at Carolina.
long_comment: Izien recorded the first sack of his career when he brought down quarterback Bryce Young for a loss of one early in the fourth quarter Sunday, and he totaled 11 tackles for the second straight game. His recent production should have put him on the IDP radar in most formats going into a Week 5 matchup at Arizona.

short_comment: Williams finished Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions with nine tackles (five solo) and one pass defense.
long_comment: As he's done in each of the first six games of the regular season, Williams was on the field for every single defensive snap Sunday, and he finished third on the Packers in tackles behind Isaiah McDuffie (11) and Xavier McKinney (10). Williams has posted at least nine tackles four times this season, and his 61 total tackles lead the Packers and is tied with Jacob Rodriguez and Payton Wilson for eighth-most in the NFL .

short_comment: McDuffie logged 11 tackles (six solo), one fumble and one fumble recovery during the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
long_comment: McDuffie was operating in an elevated role defensively due to the absence of veteran linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie answered the call by playing every single defensive snap while leading the Packers in tackles. He was credited with forcing the ball out of Jahmyr Gibbs' hands late in the second quarter, although it appeared as though it was the hand of Lions center Cade Mays that caused the fumble. However, McDuffie did land on the loose ball caused by a botched snap from Mays to Jared Goff early in the third, which the Packers' offense capitalized on with a five-play drive that ended with a 25-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to Josh Jacobs. Franklin was diagnosed with a hairline fracture in his shin, so McDuffie figures to be remain a starter on defense in the short term, with the Packers hosting the Panthers on Thursday.

short_comment: McKinney posted 10 tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions.
long_comment: Sunday was the first time since Week 17 of the 2025 season that McKinney posted double-digit tackles, and he finished second on the Packers in that category behind Isaiah McDuffie (11). McKinney has played every single defensive snap in six of seven regular-season games and is up to 31 tackles (18 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three interceptions on the year.

short_comment: Wyatt (ankle) was a limited participant during Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
long_comment: Tuesday was an upgrade from Wyatt's DNP on Monday as he works through an ankle issue that he picked up during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions. He'll have one more chance to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Panthers.

short_comment: Rhyan was diagnosed with a high ankle sprain and is expected to miss at least one month, Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com reports.
long_comment: Rhyan was injured in Sunday's loss to the Lions. To make matters worse, Jacob Monk (quadriceps) landed on injured reserve Monday, meaning the Packers may continue to rely on John Williams, the 2025 No. 250 overall pick, to fill the void at the center position for the foreseeable future.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Golden (shoulder/foot) didn't participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
long_comment: Coming out of Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions, Golden is nursing a pair of injuries that have resulted in him going down as a non-participant on the Packers' Week 8 injury report. The Packers will see if Golden can upgrade to limited or full participation in Wednesday's session before deciding whether he'll carry a designation into Thursday's game against the Panthers. Despite leading the NFL with six drops through the first seven weeks, Golden has emerged as a useful fantasy asset in his second NFL season with 36 receptions for 540 yards and three touchdowns on 69 targets to go with six rushing yards.

short_comment: Melton caught one of his two targets for four yards and logged a 24-yard kickoff return in the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
long_comment: Melton played 13 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver remains a versatile depth option for the Packers, filling in wherever he is needed without garnering much attention.

short_comment: Williams caught three passes on as many targets for 47 yards and turned two carries into four yards during the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
long_comment: Quarterback Jordan Love spread the ball around Sunday to eight different receivers, and Williams was one of five pass catchers to record at least three receptions. Williams finished fourth on the team in receiving yards, with two of his catches going for 27 and 20 yards in the first and second quarters, respectively. The second-year pro is cemented as the Packers' WR3 behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and tight end Tucker Kraft also is in the mix for looks from Love. The Packers will head back to Lambeau Field and practice on a short week for Thursday night's game against the Panthers, whose defense ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (195.7) and fifth in passing touchdowns allowed (seven).

short_comment: St-Juste (hamstring) was estimated as a full participant on Monday's practice report, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: St-Juste has missed the past two games with the injury, but his full estimation paves the way for a return Thursday night against the Panthers. The cornerback has logged one tackle across four games this season.

short_comment: The Packers placed Monk (quadriceps) on injured reserve Monday.
long_comment: A fifth-round pick in 2024, Monk started the first three games of the season at right guard and was called upon to man center Sunday against the Lions after Sean Rhyan exited with an ankle injury. With Rhyan out multiple weeks and Monk slated to miss at least four games, the Packers will likely turn to John Williams at center after he came on to play the first 58 offensive snaps of his career against Detroit on Sunday.

short_comment: Franklin suffered a hairline fracture in his shin during last Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The veteran linebacker missed Sunday's loss to the Lions and is expected to miss additional time, but coach Matt LaFleur indicated Franklin will not be placed on injured reserve. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to hold down the fort at linebacker for the Packers while Franklin is sidelined.

short_comment: Lloyd tallied six carries for 20 yards and two catches (on two targets) for 15 yards during Sunday's 20-17 loss in Detroit.
long_comment: The Packers got top RB Josh Jacobs back in the lineup for the first time this season after he spent the first six contests on the commissioner's exempt list. However, he wasn't able to provide a jolt to a moribund ground game, as the team averaged just 3.2 YPC on its 19 rushes. On a positive note for Lloyd, though, he was the only Green Bay running back other than Jacobs to earn a touch, as an active Pierre Strong did not, and Kaleb Johnson (coach's decision) was a healthy scratch. Lloyd appears set to serve as the team's No. 2 backfield option moving forward, which should provide him regular reps with which to work behind Jacobs.

short_comment: Kraft compiled four catches (on six targets) for 48 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 20-17 loss at Detroit.
long_comment: Kraft's 14-yard TD connection with QB Jordan Love late in the first quarter marked the tight end's second end-zone visit in seven games on the season. Having said that, Kraft has surpassed 50 receiving yards in just two contests, leaving him on a 29-297-2 line on 43 targets to date. WRs Matthew Golden (12 targets Sunday) and Christian Watson (eight) continue to dominate the attention of Love so far, meaning Kraft is the third option at best in the Packers' passing attack at the moment.

short_comment: Watson notched five catches (on eight targets) for 57 yards and no touchdowns during Sunday's 20-17 defeat at Detroit.
long_comment: Watson's team-high 28-yard catch in the second quarter got the Packers into the red zone for the third time in Week 7, but after a Jordan Love to Tucker Kraft TD connection on the team's second possession, Green Bay otherwise failed to score on three of four trips to premium territory. Watson himself paced the team in receiving yards Sunday, but he also wasn't able to score a TD for the third time in the last four games, leaving him sitting on six scores in seven appearances. He and his teammates have a quick turnaround with a Thursday night matchup with the Panthers on tap in Week 8.

short_comment: Love completed 27 of 45 passes for 274 yards, two touchdowns and one interception during Sunday's 20-17 loss in Detroit.
long_comment: Love and the Packers welcomed back top RB Josh Jacobs to the lineup, but season-long woes in the team's running game didn't improve, with the team averaging 3.2 YPC on its 19 carries. Head coach Matt LaFleur thus turned to the air to get the offense moving, and Love spread the ball around liberally, with nine different pass catchers being targeted, and six of those players recording at least two catches. Love now has thrown a touchdown in all seven games this season, including exactly two TDs on six occasions, but he's also sitting on a subpar 59.8 completion percentage on the campaign. He and the offense will attempt to get right Thursday night versus the Panthers.

short_comment: Smack went 1-for-3 on field-goal tries and converted both of his PATs during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions.
long_comment: Smack continued his up-and-down rookie campaign in Week 7, and he started Sunday's contest by pushing a 26-yard field-goal attempt wide right on the Packers' first possession of the game. The kicker was able to convert a 43-yard try in the fourth quarter, but he then had 35-yard try partially blocked by D.J. Wonnum with 3:25 left in regulation. Smack has now gone 6-for-11 on field-goal attempts over the last five games, and it's unclear how long the Packers will stick with him moving forward if he can't get back on track.

short_comment: Riley is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
long_comment: The Packers activated Riley from injured reserve Saturday. The defensive tackle has recovered from the Achilles tear he suffered during Week 17 of the 2025 season. Riley is set to suit up as the backup to Chris McClellan in Sunday's divisional contest against the Lions.

short_comment: Johnson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions.
long_comment: Johnson is inactive one week after logging eight carries for 42 yards in the Packers' Week 6 win over the Buccaneers. The running back has likely been sidelined due to a crucial fourth-quarter fumble, combined with the return of Josh Jacobs from the Commissioner's Exemption List.

short_comment: Al-Shaair recorded nine tackles (two solo) in a Week 7 overtime loss to the Giants on Sunday.
long_comment: Al-Shaair battled a knee injury during Week 7 prep but seemed to be fine Sunday, as he played every one of Houston's defensive snaps. The veteran linebacker has been a consistent producer this season, logging at least seven stops in each of the six contests in which he's played. Al-Shaair posted 103 tackles over 16 regular-season games last year, and he's on pace to easily surpass that mark with 58 stops through six contests this season.

short_comment: To'oTo'o notched 10 tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, in Sunday's Week 7 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: To'oTo'o ranked second on Houston in tackles behind M.J. Stewart, with whom he combined for a sack in the fourth quarter. It was just the third appearance of the campaign for To'oTo'o, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 due to a knee injury. The 25-year-old seems to be past the issue, as he's logged more than 90 percent of the Texans' defensive snaps since his return.

short_comment: Stewart finished with 12 tackles (five solo), including 0.5 sacks, and a defensed pass in Sunday's overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Stewart paced Houston in tackles, and he contributed a half-sack of J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter. Stewart missed the first four weeks of the campaign due to a knee injury and was limited to work on special teams upon his return in Week 5, but he started and logged a 95 percent defensive snap share Sunday in the absence of Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand). The Texans are on bye in Week 8, so Blankenship will have extra time to recover ahead of Houston's Week 9 matchup against the Chargers.
