short_comment: Moreau played 21 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in the Texans' 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants on Sunday.
long_comment: Moreau did not appear in the box score of Sunday's game. The tight end's complete lack of offensive production was in stark contrast to his Week 6 two-touchdown effort against the Jaguars in London, and Moreau's week-to-week production figures to remain erratic while working behind clear No. 1 option Dalton Schultz.

short_comment: Ogunbowale didn't record an offensive touch or target in Sunday's 24-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Even with David Montgomery (groin) and Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) injured and inactive, Ogunbowale played just seven offensive snaps behind Woody Marks' 54. Ogunbowale can continue to be ignored in fantasy football.

short_comment: Dell caught his only target for 43 yards and added a two-yard rush during Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Dell made his return to action after missing nearly two full years while recovering from a dislocated kneecap and a series of torn ligaments in his left knee. The wide receiver was on the field for only 11 offensive plays, but he made the most of his one target. Dell reeled in a deep ball from C.J. Stroud in the second quarter, churning out a 43-yard gain. With Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel (toe) and Kayshon Boutte also in the mix at wide receiver, Dell may have a hard time getting many looks each week.

short_comment: Boutte caught one of two targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss versus the Giants.
long_comment: Boutte played a season-low 18 offensive snaps in Week 7, trailing behind Nico Collins (34) and Xavier Hutchinson (31) and tying with Jaylin Noel (toe). Predictably, Boutte wasn't very involved in an inefficient passing game. As recent trade acquisition Marvin Harrison gets acclimated, Boutte's role probably will continue to shrink as the campaign continues.

short_comment: Schultz caught five of six targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: The veteran tight end paced the Texans with his six targets, matching Xavier Hutchinson, as the duo saw one more than Nico Collins on a day when C.J. Stroud targeted nine different pass catchers. Schultz is still looking for his first touchdown of the season and has settled in as a low-ceiling fantasy tight end.

short_comment: Hutchinson caught three of six targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants. He added 12 rushing yards on two attempts.
long_comment: On a day in which C.J. Stroud targeted nine different players, Hutchinson tied Dalton Schultz for the team lead with six targets. Nico Collins led the wideout group with 24 routes, but Hutchinson tied Jaylin Noel (toe) for second at the position with 15 routes. In a receiver room that is running six deep on game days, none of these Houston wide receivers are reliably playable in fantasy outside of Collins.

short_comment: Fairbairn went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and converted his only PAT in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Fairbairn finished off each of the Texans' first two scoring drives with field-goal makes from 58 and 57 yards in the first half. The kicker has now converted multiple field goals in four straight contests, and his last miss came all the way back in Week 2 versus Cincinnati. Fairbairn has gone 15-for-16 on field-goal tries, including 6-for-7 from 50-plus yards, while making all 16 of his extra-point attempts over seven contests so far.

short_comment: Harrison caught one of four targets for a six-yard touchdown in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: In his second game since being acquired from Arizona via trade, Harrison scored his first touchdown with the Texans. His six-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter was Harrison's lone catch in a game during which six different wide receivers recorded at least one reception for the Texans. Harrison will have an opportunity to increase his knowledge of the playbook during a Week 8 bye and potentially earn more playing time in Houston's crowded wide-receiver room.

short_comment: Stroud completed 17 of 28 passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants. He added two rushing attempts for four yards and threw a successful two-point conversion.
long_comment: Stroud threw a six-yard touchdown pass to Marvin Harrison in the final minute of the first half and added a two-point conversion to Cade Stover to tie the score at 14-14 heading into halftime. Houston's next points didn't come until the final minute of the fourth quarter, when Stroud found Xavier Hutchinson for a three-yard touchdown that sent the game to overtime. The Texans went three-and-out on the first possession of OT, and the Giants responded with a touchdown to drop the Texans to 2-5 heading into Houston's Week 8 bye. It's hard to blame Stroud for the team's poor record given his strong 11:1 TD:INT.

short_comment: Marks rushed 19 times for 66 yards and caught his only target for 15 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Mark remained busy in the absence of David Montgomery (groin), handling 20 touches while no other running back got a touch for the Texans. Over the last three games, the first of which Montgomery left early and the last two of which he missed, Marks has recorded 247 scrimmage yards on 56 touches. Marks missed some action in the second half Sunday due to a leg injury but returned to the game. Houston's Week 8 bye will give both Marks and Montgomery a chance to heal up, and Houston would likely return to a backfield platoon in Week 9 against the Chargers if Montgomery's ready to play.

short_comment: Collins caught two of five targets for six yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
long_comment: Collins was surprisingly quiet as C.J. Stroud spread the ball out to nine different targets, including six wide receivers. Collins remains atop the wide-receiver depth chart and hadn't dipped below 55 receiving yards in a regular-season appearance since Week 7 of last season. The star wideout's recent track record suggests Collins will likely bounce back in Week 9 against the Chargers following Houston's Week 8 bye.

short_comment: Noel (toe) was seen in a walking boot after Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Noel suffered a toe injury in the fourth quarter of Week 7 action and didn't return, finishing with two catches (on two targets) for minus-3 yards. He wasn't able to parlay his 107-yard outing from Week 6 against the Jaguars in London into any success this Sunday, and he now be in danger of missing time.

short_comment: Jordan (foot) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
long_comment: Jordan likely sustained his foot injury during Thursday's practice, but the tight end was quickly able to upgrade to a full participant in Friday's practice. Jordan is all set to suit up as a depth option at tight end in Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Davis-Gaither recorded seven tackles (three solo) in Sunday's loss to Minnesota.
long_comment: Davis-Gaither's tackle total was good for second on Indianapolis behind A.J. Haulcy. Davis-Gaither has established a very reliable fantasy floor with at least seven stops in all seven of his appearances so far this season. He ranks 12th in the league with 60 tackles on the campaign.

short_comment: Adebawore finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with five tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a defensed pass.
long_comment: The Vikings have stood out this season for their ability to get to the passer, but Adebawore gave them some of their own medicine Sunday. He brought down Kyler Murray twice in the fourth quarter as Indianapolis tried to stage a comeback. Adebawore is up to 4.0 sacks through seven games, so he's already tied the career-best regular-season mark he established last year.

short_comment: Haulcy produced nine tackles (five solo) in a loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
long_comment: The game was mostly centered on defense, and Haulcy helped Indianapolis hang close with a team-leading nine stops. That was a season-best mark for the rookie safety, who has taken on a starting role in his debut NFL campaign. Haulcy has logged 36 tackles and two defensed passes through seven contests.

short_comment: The Colts placed Taylor-Britt on injured reserve Tuesday due to a groin injury, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
long_comment: Taylor-Britt suffered the injury on the first play of the fourth quarter of Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings. It's another blow to the Colts' secondary, given that the team was without Sauce Gardner (calf) during Sunday's game, and fellow defensive back Justin Walley sustained a knee injury during the contest. Taylor-Britt will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29. Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken are both in line for more defensive snaps in the absence of Taylor-Britt.

short_comment: Giddens did not play a single snap during Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Giddens dressed for Sunday's game, but he observed the entire contest from the sidelines while Seth McGowan served as the Colts' lone backup to Jonathan Taylor. Giddens has yet to play a snap this regular season, but that could change if the Colts -- who have a 2-5 record -- are sellers at the trade deadline and opt to send Taylor to another team.

short_comment: Mallory did not catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota.
long_comment: Mallory and the other Colts tight ends worked in larger roles offensively Sunday due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). However, the former's 21 offensive snaps ranked third behind Mo Alie-Cox (39) and Drew Ogletree (35), and Mallory could not connect with Daniel Jones, with the third and final pass that came his way resulting in an interception by Harrison Smith. Mallory has seen nine targets over his last two games since coming off injured reserve, but his role would shrink against the Jaguars in Week 8 if Warren is given the green light to play in that contest.

short_comment: Alie-Cox failed to haul in either of his targets during the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
long_comment: Alie-Cox led all Colts tight ends with 39 offensive snaps, but he could not connect with Daniel Jones on two pass attempts from the veteran quarterback. Alie-Cox and the other Indianapolis tight ends were operating in elevated roles for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). Alie-Cox's snap count would take a hit if Warren was cleared to return for Week 8 against Jacksonville.

short_comment: Ogletree caught both of his passes for 12 yards during the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
long_comment: Ogletree and the other Colts tight ends stepped into larger roles offensively for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). Ogletree's 35 offensive snaps were second most among Indianapolis' tight ends, and he set season highs in catches, targets and receiving yards. He's mostly worked as a blocker on offense, and his snap count would be lower in Week 8 against the Jaguars if Warren is cleared to return for that contest.

short_comment: Treadwell caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
long_comment: Treadwell played 45 offensive snaps in Sunday's loss. The wide receiver participated in 74 percent of the Colts' offensive plays, but the No. 3 option saw fewer targets than Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

short_comment: McGowan turned 11 carries into 46 yards, caught his only target for two yards and added 140 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: McGowan played a season-high 31 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and as a result, he was able to set new highs in both carries and rushing yards. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded in the coming weeks, the rookie would stand to operate as the team's lead back following Taylor's departure. On the season, McGowan has rushed 34 times for 134 yards and reeled in four of five targets for 12 yards while compiling 566 kickoff-return yards over seven contests so far.

short_comment: Allen caught all three of his targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Allen was held to his fewest catches, receiving yards and targets since Week 2 as the Colts struggled to establish a passing attack against Minnesota's impressive defense. The wide receiver still led the team in all three categories, and he'll have a chance for better production in Week 8 versus the Jaguars.

short_comment: According to head coach Shane Steichen, Walley did not return to Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota due to a knee injury, Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
long_comment: Walley exited the Week 7 meeting with the Vikings in the third quarter and did not return. Until there is a more definitive update on his condition, he should be considered questionable ahead of Sunday's game versus the Jaguars. If Walley can't suit up for that contest, Cam Taylor-Britt (groin) and Kapena Gushiken are candidates for more snaps.

short_comment: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) will "most likely not" have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 8, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
long_comment: A couple weeks ago, Pierce shed the cast that he had been wearing to protect his surgically repaired left heel, but the wideout looks like he'll remain limited to rehab work for at least another week before potentially making his return to practice. In Pierce's continued absence, the Colts will lean on Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell to serve as their primary receiver trio, though none of the three have been consistent fantasy producers while quarterback Daniel Jones (4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has struggled mightily through the first seven weeks of the season.

short_comment: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that Jones will remain the team's starting quarterback in Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports.
long_comment: Though the Colts have limped out to a disappointing 2-5 start to the season, Steichen reiterated that he has confidence in Jones, who signed a two-year, $88 million extension in March after his inaugural campaign in Indianapolis was cut short by a torn Achilles tendon. As expected, Jones hasn't provided much of an impact as a runner (21 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown) coming off major surgery, but his significant regression as a passer (59.6 percent completion rate, 4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has impeded the Indianapolis offense. While his contract should give Jones some level of security, another poor performance or two could compel the Colts to give 2023 first-round pick Anthony Richardson another look under center.

short_comment: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Shrader entered Week 7 without having missed a field-goal try over the team's first six contests, but he was unable to remain perfect. The kicker was able to make a 43-yard field goal as time expired in the first half, giving Indianapolis a 10-6 lead at the break. Shrader then missed a 56-yard try wide left in the third quarter before pushing a 48-yard attempt wide right in the fourth quarter. He has now gone 19-for-21 on field-goal tries while making 13 of 14 extra-point attempts over seven contests this season.

short_comment: Downs caught two of four targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Daniel Jones couldn't get anything going at all through the air against the Minnesota defense, and Downs' four targets actually led Indianapolis, although he didn't accomplish much with that modest volume. The two grabs and four targets tied his season lows, and Downs has been held under 20 receiving yards in two of the last four games, and under 50 in all four. Unless Jones can shake himself out of his stupor, Downs' ceiling will remain very limited in a Week 8 tilt against the Jaguars.

short_comment: Taylor carried the ball 18 times for 95 yards and a touchdown and caught two of three targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The Colts managed only 218 yards of offense in total, and Taylor had nearly as many rushing yards as Daniel Jones had passing yards. Taylor also scored his team's only TD on a 38-year-old dash in the first quarter. The star RB is still looking for his first 100-yard rushing performance of the season, but he's topped 90 yards in five of seven games and has produced 100-plus scrimmage yards four times while racking up eight scores on the ground. Taylor will face another tough run defense in Week 8 versus the Jaguars.

short_comment: Sanchez (foot) no longer holds any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: Sanchez injured his foot during the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans when his punt was blocked and returned for a touchdown. The punter and holder has recovered from the injury just in time to suit up for Sunday's contest against the Vikings.

short_comment: Harrison was diagnosed with a torn ACL while undergoing a procedure on his right knee Thursday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: The Jaguars were hoping that Harrison was undergoing just an arthroscopic procedure, but the surgeons found more damage than originally thought. As such, the 2023 first-rounder will miss the rest of the season, and how he progresses in his recovery over the coming months will determine whether he will be available for the start of the 2027 campaign. Walker Little figures to start at left tackle in Harrison's absence.

short_comment: Oluokun logged eight tackles (four solo) in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans in London on Sunday.
long_comment: Oluokun did not have an outstanding game by any metrics but did put up a solid stat line in a close divisional loss. The linebacker played 94 percent of the Jaguars' defensive snaps in the contest while logging an additional 24 percent of the team's snaps on special teams. Oluokun leads the Jaguars with 42 tackles on the season.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Cameron didn't garner a target and recorded 46 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: Cameron went without a target for the first time since Week 2, but he did play a season-high 50 percent of the team's offensive snaps. The wide receiver played 19 more snaps on offense than Brian Thomas, and he appears to have officially taken over as the team's No. 3 option behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers at his position. On the year, Cameron has caught eight of 12 targets for 117 yards and two touchdowns while also adding 245 yards as a kick returner over six games.

short_comment: Little made his sole field-goal attempt and all four of his PATs in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans on Sunday in London.
long_comment: Little made a 60-yard field goal with 1:55 left in the fourth quarter to tie the game, 31-31. The Jaguars' kicker continues to deliver in big moments for the team whenever called upon. Little moves to 10-for-12 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-17 on PATs through six games in 2026.

short_comment: Boerkircher caught both of his targets for eight yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: Boerkircher was able to find pay dirt for the first time in his NFL career, reeling in a one-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the fourth quarter. The 25-year-old now has gathered in six of eight targets for 52 yards and a touchdown over six contests to open the regular season.

short_comment: Strange caught five of seven targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: Strange finished tied for the team lead in catches with wide receiver Jakobi Meyers, while his seven targets were third behind Meyers (10) and Parker Washington (11). The tight end has now reeled in at least five passes in three straight contests, compiling 207 receiving yards on 19 catches in those games. The Jaguars are off in Week 7, so his next chance to continue his momentum will come Nov. 1 against the Colts.

short_comment: Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards while failing to reel in his only target during Sunday's 34-31 loss to Houston.
long_comment: Rodriguez led the team in rushing yards, out-producing fellow running back Bhayshul Tuten's 39 yards on 12 carries. Although the two split the carries almost evenly, Tuten caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two scores in the contest. Rodriguez has now compiled 168 yards on 39 carries while catching one pass for six yards over six contests to open the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Hunter caught all four of his targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London. He also recorded three tackles and an interception.
long_comment: The two-way player is beginning to flash the talent that made him the second overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Hunter's receiving numbers were by far a season high -- he had only two catches coming into Sunday -- and his day on offense was capped by a seven-yard touchdown reception from Trevor Lawrence in the fourth quarter that brought the Jaguars to within a field goal at 31-28. Hunter then made an impact on the very next possession, picking off a C.J. Stroud pass in the end zone with just under four minutes left on the clock to keep his team in the game. The touchdown and interception were each the second of his career in his 13th NFL game, and Hunter became the first player since 2002 to have one of each in the same game. Jacksonville's receiver room is crowded with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas at the top of the depth chart, but head coach Liam Coen hinted after the game that Hunter's role on offense could continue to grow following the team's Week 7 bye, per CBS 47 Jacksonville.

short_comment: Thomas didn't haul in either of his two targets during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London.
long_comment: Per Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com, Thomas logged 15 offensive snaps in the first half but none after halftime, while all of fellow wideouts Parker Washington (11 targets), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Travis Hunter (four) had major roles in the Jaguars offense. Thomas maintained a regular workload in the first five games of the season, with his snap shares ranging from 35 to 62 percent en route to a 9-105-1 line on 18 targets. Sunday's development could be a sign of things to come for Thomas without the team mentioning any sort of injury during or after Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Meyers caught five of 10 targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: While Parker Washington led the Jaguars with 11 looks from Trevor Lawrence, Meyers paced the club in catches and receiving yards on his largest target volume of the season. The 83 yards were also a season best for Meyers, and the veteran wideout will take a 20-285-2 line on 28 targets into a bye before clashing with the Colts in Week 8.

short_comment: Washington caught four of 11 targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: Despite leading the Jaguars in targets, Washington finished second to Jakobi Meyers in both catches and receiving yards, and he wasn't on the other end of any of Trevor Lawrence's four TDs. It's the third time in the last four games that Washington has failed to reach five grabs or 70 yards, but the fourth contest featured a 6-124-2 line from the fourth-year wideout. Washington will take a 26-416-4 line on 46 targets into a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

short_comment: Lawrence completed 24 of 41 passes for 306 yards and four touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
long_comment: The Jaguars had to open things up in the second half after falling behind 24-14 following the Texans' first possession of the third quarter, and Lawrence wound up attempting 40-plus passes for the first time this season while tying his 2026 high in TD passes with two scores to Bhayshul Tuten, and one each to Travis Hunter and rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher. He also topped 300 passing yards for a second straight game. Lawrence will take a 14:4 TD:INT into a bye before clashing with the Colts in Week 8.

short_comment: Tuten carried the ball 12 times for 39 yards and caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
long_comment: While the Houston front seven kept him bottled up on the ground -- Tuten's longest run went for just five yards -- the second-year RB made an impact through the air, turning a dump pass from Trevor Lawrence into a 27-yard score in the second quarter before catching another two-yard TD before halftime. The receiving touchdowns were his first of the season and tied his total from all of 2025, and Tuten topped 80 scrimmage yards for the fourth straight game. The Jaguars will get a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

short_comment: Johnson (ankle) didn't return to second half of Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans, Brent Martineau of CBS 47 Jacksonville reports.
long_comment: The Jaguars had listed Johnson as questionable to return after he left in the second quarter due to the ankle injury, but though he was spotted on the sideline in the second half, he never checked back into the contest. Kaevon Merriweather ended up serving as the primary replacement at safety for Johnson, who will have a Week 7 bye to recover from his injury before potentially returning to action Nov. 1 versus the Colts. Johnson accrued six tackles prior to his departure.

short_comment: Murray (concussion) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.
long_comment: Murray has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game. The strong safety has been cleared for full contact by an independent neurologist and is all set to suit up alongside Jaguars' free safety Antonio Johnson when the team takes on the Texans.

short_comment: Conner finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to Seattle with seven tackles (two solo).
long_comment: Conner was on the field for every single defensive snap for a second consecutive game following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye. He missed the first three games of the regular season due to a knee injury but has suited up for each of the team's last three contests, during which he has accumulated 17 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense.

short_comment: Williams finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 10 tackles (four solo) and one interception.
long_comment: The second-year defensive back's 10 tackles were a career best, and his interception off Sam Darnold late in the second quarter was also the first of Williams' NFL career. Williams is up to 29 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through six regular-season games.

short_comment: Bolton registered 11 tackles (six solo) during the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
long_comment: Bolton played all but one of the Chiefs' 69 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he finished second on the team in tackles behind Drue Tranquill (12). Bolton has recorded double-digit stops in four of six regular-season games and is up to 59 tackles (29 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.

short_comment: Tranquill finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 12 tackles (four solo).
long_comment: Tranquil led the Chiefs in combined tackles Sunday, and he was one of three Kansas City defenders to reach double-digit stops. He's logged at least seven tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 48 tackles (22 solo), two pass defenses and one fumble recovery in 2026.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Armstrong caught one of two targets for three yards during Sunday night's 20-3 loss to Seattle.
long_comment: Armstrong was signed to the active roster ahead of Week 7, and he was on the field for 56 percent of the team's offensive snaps. With Rashee Rice (hamstring) still banged up, it's possible that Armstrong operates in a similar role in Week 8 versus Denver.

short_comment: Allen caught one of two targets for 18 yards during the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
long_comment: Allen and QB Patrick Mahomes connected on an 18-yard pass on the Chiefs' second offensive play of the game, but the rookie wide receiver did not see another pass from his veteran quarterback until the fourth quarter. All three of Allen's catches this season have come over his last two games, which has coincided with the absence of Rashee Rice (knee/hamstring). Allen was on the field for 16 of the Chiefs' 53 offensive snaps Sunday, and his minimal role will decrease even more if Rice is cleared to return for Week 8 against the Broncos on Nov. 1.

short_comment: Gray caught three passes on as many targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Gray and Travis Kelce ended up tied for the most receiving yards on the Chiefs on Sunday, although the offense struggled as a whole, with Patrick Mahomes throwing for only 165 yards and Kenneth Walker averaging only 2.6 yards per carry. Gray has caught 11 of 12 passes for 153 yards over his last four games, though he's limited to a complementary role in the passing game behind Kelce, Xavier Worthy and, when healthy, Rashee Rice (knee/hamstring). The Chiefs will stay on the road for Week 8 against the Broncos, whose defense ranks 24th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to tight ends.

short_comment: Johnson caught two of three passes for 17 yards and returned three kickoffs for 81 yards during Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. He also added two tackles on special teams.
long_comment: Johnson was held without a carry for the second time in three games, with lead back Kenneth Walker bottled up for 36 yards on 14 carries (2.6 YPC). Johnson has seen three carries or fewer in four of the first six games of the regular season and figures to be limited to a third-down role as a pass catcher unless Walker misses time. The Chiefs will stay on the road for a Week 8 divisional matchup against the Broncos on Nov. 1.

short_comment: Butker went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts during Sunday night's 20-3 loss to Seattle.
long_comment: Butker was off his game again in Week 7, leaving a 58-yard attempt short as time expired in the first half before later missing a 45-yard try wide right in the fourth quarter. The kicker was able to convert one field-goal attempt Sunday, nailing a 50-yarder in the third quarter. Butker has now gone 11-for-16 on field-goal attempts, including 2-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over the first six contests of the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Worthy caught three of six targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Seattle successfully limited Worthy's output in the absence of Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), with the versatile Nick Emmanwori running stride for stride with the speedy Worthy on a couple of downfield misconnections. Worthy finished second behind Travis Kelce (eight) in targets but sixth on the Chiefs in receiving yards Sunday. Heading into a Week 8 road game against the Broncos, Worthy has drawn at least six targets in five of six games this season. He has reached 70 yards twice and failed to eclipse 25 yards in any of the other four games.

short_comment: Kelce caught four of eight targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Kelce increased his career total to 1,104 regular-season catches, passing Hall of Famers Marvin Harrison (1,102) and Cris Carter (1,101) to move up to fifth on the all-time list. Jason Witten holds the fourth spot with 1,228 receptions, so Kelce is more likely to be caught by Keenan Allen (1,084) than Kelce is to catch Witten. Kelce led the Chiefs with eight targets in the absence of WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and tied fellow TE Noah Gray for the team lead in receiving yards as Kansas City mustered just three Harrison Butker field-goal attempts on offense, two of which missed. This was only the second time Kelce failed to reach the 50-yard threshold in six appearances this season. He had 71 yards in Week 1 against the Broncos, whom the Chiefs will face in a Week 8 road rematch.

short_comment: Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. He added two rushing attempts for 14 yards.
long_comment: Mahomes was picked off in the second quarter and remarkably recovered his own fumble in a pile of bodies to avoid a second turnover in the third quarter, setting up a Harrison Butker field goal on the next play for the Chiefs' only points of the night. This was the first start in Mahomes' career during which Kansas City failed to reach the red zone, and he hasn't thrown a touchdown pass in two games since KC's Week 5 bye. Seattle's defense dominated while Kansas City struggled to move the ball in the absence of No. 1 WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), whom the Chiefs will hope to get back for a Week 8 road game against the Broncos.

short_comment: Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards while catching four of five targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Walker was held in check by his former team after recording at least 70 rushing yards in each of his first five games with the Chiefs. The MVP of Super LX with Seattle entered play Sunday leading the league with 665 rushing yards on 6.3 yards per carry in the 2026 regular season, but he mustered just 2.6 YPC in by far his quietest performance of the season against a Seahawks defense that hasn't allowed a 100-yard rushing performance since Week 8 of the 2024 regular season. Walker has a nice bounce-back opportunity in a Week 8 road clash with the Broncos, against whom he generated 191 scrimmage yards and two total touchdowns in the season opener.

short_comment: Sneed (knee) is active for Sunday night's game against the Seahawks.
long_comment: Sneed stayed back in Kansas City due to personal reasons but flew out on his own this weekend and is good to go for Sunday night. The veteran cornerback has appeared in all five games this season, logging 30 tackles (20 solo), three pass breakups and two forced fumbles.

short_comment: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday night's game against the Seahawks.
long_comment: The rookie seventh-round pick continues to sit behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields to begin the season.

short_comment: The Chiefs activated McDonald (knee) from injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: The Chiefs opened McDonald's 21-day practice window Oct. 20. The reserve linebacker has recovered from his knee injury and should be all set to suit up for Sunday Night Football against the Seahawks.

short_comment: The Chiefs placed Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Smith sustained a hamstring injury in Thursday's practice session and has promptly been transitioned to IR as he manages the issue. Running back Jaydn Ott has been signed to the active roster to be the No. 3 option behind Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson while Smith recovers.

short_comment: The Chiefs signed Ott from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: The Chiefs placed Brashard Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday in a corresponding move. Smith's injury leaves an opportunity for Ott. The undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma could make his NFL debut during Sunday Night Football as the Chiefs take on the Seahawks in Week 7.

short_comment: The Chiefs placed Simmons (lower back) on injured reserve Thursday.
long_comment: Though he had been on the Chiefs' 53-man roster all season, Simmons had yet to make his 2026 debut while working his way back from a bulging and herniated disc in his lower back. Simmons appeared to be making strides in his recovery after he returned to practice last week as a limited participant, but he downgraded to no participation Wednesday after head trainer Rick Burkholder said that the second-year left tackle "plateaued in the rehab process," per Nate Taylor of ESPN.com. As a result, the Chiefs have opted to deactivate Simmons, who won't be eligible to play until Week 11 versus the Cardinals. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson should continue to start at left tackle in Simmons' absence.

short_comment: Karlaftis registered six total tackles, a sack and two pass breakups in Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers.
long_comment: Though Sunday's contest marked the first time all season that he notched a sack, Karlaftis has been making life difficult on quarterbacks throughout the campaign. Per Pro Football Focus, Karlaftis ranks seventh in the NFL with 27 total quarterback pressures, including 19 over the Chiefs' past two games. Karlaftis has also tallied 21 tackles, four pass breakups and an interception through five appearances.

short_comment: Chinn finished Sunday's Week 7 loss to the Rams with seven tackles (three solo). He also recovered a fumble.
long_comment: Chinn tied for third on Las Vegas in stops and has now registered at least seven tackles in four of his seven games so far this season. The veteran safety also came up with a big fumble recovery in Rams territory in the third quarter, but the Raiders were unable to turn that into points. Chinn has 46 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, one defensed pass, two forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles through seven contests on the campaign.

short_comment: Walker posted 12 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's Week 7 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: Walker and Nakobe Dean each had 12 tackles to tie for the team lead. Two of Walker's stops went for a loss. The tackle tally was a season-best mark for the veteran linebacker and marked the second time in 2026 that he's posted double-digit stops. In his first year with the Raiders, Walker has registered 52 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and a recovered fumble through seven contests.

short_comment: Dean produced 12 tackles and an interception in Sunday's loss to the Rams.
long_comment: Dean tied with Quay Walker for the team lead in tackles and also came up with an interception of Matthew Stafford early in the fourth quarter. That helped set up a Raiders touchdown, but Las Vegas ultimately suffered a third straight loss. Dean is in the midst of a standout season, as he's recorded double-digit stops in four of his past five games and is tied for third in the NFL with 68 tackles through seven contests.

short_comment: The Raiders reinstated Thornton (hamstring) from injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: With Thornton's 21-day practice window coming to a close this week, the Raiders elected to move him back on to the 53-man roster. A full participant in each of the Raiders' last nine practices, Thornton looks like he'll be ready to play this Sunday against the Jets, but he may not be in store for a meaningful role in the receiver rotation. He struggled to carve out consistent volume in the passing game as a rookie fourth-round pick in 2025, putting together a 10-135-0 receiving line on 30 targets over 15 appearances.

short_comment: White caught one of three targets for four yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: White has now posted back-to-back duds, totaling one catch for four yards on five targets across the last two contests. In an offense that doesn't often use three wide receivers on the field at once, White is pretty clearly behind both Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor for snaps and routes. White ran just nine routes on Kirk Cousins' 48 dropbacks in Week 7.

short_comment: Mendoza did not appear in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: Mendoza didn't see any action for the second straight week after he got his toes wet in the team's Week 5 loss to New England. With the Raiders falling to 3-4 with the loss in Week 7, current starting quarterback Kirk Cousins may not remain in that role for much longer. Las Vegas will travel to face the Jets in Week 8 before a trio of tough matchups against the 49ers, Seahawks and Broncos in the ensuing three weeks.

short_comment: Nailor caught two of five targets for 14 yards during Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: Nailor was able to reel in multiple passes for the first time since Week 1, but he was still limited to an uninspiring 14 receiving yards. With Brock Bowers, Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty combining for 28 targets in the contest, Nailor operated as the No. 4 option at best for Las Vegas. Through six contests this year, the wide receiver has caught eight of 20 targets for 75 yards, and he is still searching for his first touchdown.

short_comment: The Raiders designated Bech (forearm) for return from injured reserve Monday.
long_comment: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Bech can practice with the team while the Raiders evaluate him for a potential return to the 53-man roster. Before fracturing his left forearm in a Week 3 win over the Saints, Bech had recorded five receptions for 48 yards and a touchdown on six targets while serving as the Raiders' No. 3 wideout behind Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor.

short_comment: Head coach Klint Kubiak said that Cousins will remain the Raiders' starting quarterback heading into Sunday's game against the Jets, Paul Gutierrez of the team's official site reports. "There is no controversy," Kubiak said. "He is playing at a very high level."
long_comment: Though the Raiders have dropped four straight games to drop to 3-4 on the season, Kubiak reaffirmed his commitment to Cousins, who has done his part to keep the team competitive amid the losing streak. The veteran signal-caller leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes and ranks third with 1,877 passing yards, with the Raiders' struggling defense (28.1 points allowed per game) and poor running game (3.0 yards per carry) having been the bigger culprits in the team's recent swoon. According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Kubiak said that No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is "going to play at some point," but the rookie looks like he'll have to wait at least one more week before seeing extended action while Cousins has directed a serviceable offense.

short_comment: Tucker secured five of 12 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
long_comment: Tucker led the Raiders in receiving yards and targets on the afternoon with a big lift from a game-long 41-yard catch and a 37-yard fourth-quarter touchdown reception. The speedy wideout has a combined 10-200-3 line over his last two games alone as he continues to take his chemistry with Kirk Cousins to new levels, and Tucker is averaging a stellar 16.3 yards per reception heading into a favorable Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

short_comment: Mayer caught all three targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: After a big Week 6 in which Mayer caught seven of nine targets for 95 yards against the Bills, Mayer faded into the background against Los Angeles, as Tre Tucker (5-103-1 receiving), Brock Bowers (6-73-0) and Ashton Jeanty (8-61-1) accounted for most of the production in the passing game for the Raiders. Mayer will be a fantasy TE1/2 for next Sunday's game against the Jets.

short_comment: Washington rushed six times for 27 yards in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: Despite dealing with foot and back injuries throughout the practice week, Washington played against Los Angeles and handled his normal workload behind starter Ashton Jeanty. Even though Jeanty again handled more carries, Washington ended up leading the team in rushing yards on a day the Raiders ran for just 48 yards. Washington is pushing Jeanty for more rushing work, but it's not enough at this point to warrant starting the rookie running back in fantasy.

short_comment: Jeanty rushed eight times for 15 yards and brought in all eight targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
long_comment: The Rams stonewalled Jeanty on the ground, but the 2025 first-round pick was highly effective as a receiver. Jeanty led the Raiders in receptions and tied for second in targets, and his 15-yard grab came when the running back ran past Kam Curl down the right sideline early in the fourth quarter. Jeanty has been held under 30 rushing yards in three straight games, but he's up to a 34-312-3 receiving line on 44 targets going into a Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

short_comment: Bowers secured six of eight targets for 73 yards in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
long_comment: The ultra-talented tight end put together another solid performance, finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for the Raiders while also tying for runner-up status in targets. Bowers has at least 70 receiving yards in all five of the games in which he's played, and he's recorded at least six catches in four of those contests. Bowers will undoubtedly  remain a critical part of the air attack in a Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

short_comment: Johnson (stinger/neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Rams.
long_comment: Johnson suffered a similar injury in Week 5 versus the Patriots, and his status for the rest of Week 7 is now in question. The linebacker is primarily a special-teams asset, so his absence doesn't carry much of an impact on defense versus Los Angeles.

short_comment: Thomas (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's contest against the Rams, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Thomas is back in action after briefly being sidelined with a shoulder injury that he suffered early in the game. He'll continue to operate as a depth option at tight end behind Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer versus Los Angeles.

short_comment: O'Connell (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Raiders' emergency third quarterback against the Rams on Sunday.
long_comment: O'Connell will only enter Sunday's game if both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza must exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: The Raiders have ruled out Runyon (foot) for Sunday's game against the Rams.
long_comment: Runyon was a full participant in practice throughout the week, after he had been limited in the Raiders' three Week 6 sessions upon having his 21-day window opened Oct. 14. If the tight end can remain free of restrictions in practices during Week 8 prep, he'll stand a good chance of being activated from injured reserve ahead of the Raiders' Nov. 1 matchup with the Jets.

short_comment: Hemingway (concussion) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.
long_comment: Hemingway was unable to play against the Bills in Week 6 while in the league's concussion protocol. He strung together a DNP-LP-FP practice log during Week 7 prep, and he's cleared protocol after passing tests administered by an independent neurologist. Hemingway's return will bolster the Raiders' defensive line, with Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi reverting to rotational roles.

short_comment: McConkey (concussion) was spotted on the field in a no-contact jersey during the Chargers' bonus practice session Monday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: After a Week 7 bye, the Chargers held an unofficial practice Monday as they begin prepping for a road matchup with the Rams next Sunday. Though the team won't have to release its first Week 8 injury report Wednesday, McConkey appears poised to be listed as at least a limited practice participant, which suggests that he's made some progress through the five-step concussion protocol. The wideout will look to practice fully by the end of the week and receive clearance from an independent neurologist in order to play against the Rams.

short_comment: Thompson (quadriceps) was active but didn't play any snaps Sunday in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: After sitting out the Chargers' previous three games due to the quad issue, Thompson was listed as questionable heading into Sunday's contest after three limited practices. Though he got the green light to suit up, Thompson was presumably available only in an emergency since the Chargers' seven-man inactive list consisted of players who were dealing with more significant injuries. Thompson will have added time to get healthy while the Chargers are on bye Week 7, and if he can fully practice at some point during Week 8, he'll have a good chance at seeing his first game action since Week 2 in the team's Nov. 1 matchup with the Rams.

short_comment: Lambert-Smith caught five of nine targets for 32 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss at Kansas City. He also lost a fumble.
long_comment: Lambert-Smith drew 12 targets total over 10 games during his rookie season in 2025, so his involvement in Week 6 is eyebrow-raising. His 59 offensive snaps actually paced the Chargers' wide receivers Sunday, with Tre' Harris (hamstring) sidelined and Ladd McConkey knocked out of the contest early by a concussion. Offensive Coordinator Mike McDaniel notoriously covets players with breakaway speed, which Lambert-Smith definitely possesses (4.37-second 40-yard dash), so despite his putting the ball on the ground Sunday, McDaniel may continue to try to find ways to get Lambert-Smith involved as the campaign progresses.

short_comment: Dicker made both of his field-goal attempts in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
long_comment: Dicker's 23-yard and 30-yard field goals were the only points scored by the Chargers in the team's blowout loss. While the offense could not get going, as has been the theme all season, Dicker remained reliable. The 26-year-old moves to 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts over six regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: Kolar caught three of six targets for 20 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
long_comment: Kolar finished fifth on the Chargers in receiving yards, but he was also second on the team in both catches and targets behind KeAndre Lambert-Smith (five catches on nine targets for 32 yards). Kolar has a 6-57-0 receiving line in his two outings since returning from a two-game absence due to a fractured forearm, but he's stuck in an offense that is one of the worst units in the league this season. The Chargers will look to regroup during the Week 7 bye before facing the Rams in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Vidal turned seven carries into 21 yards and caught three of four passes for 19 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
long_comment: The Chargers' run offense struggled Sunday, but Vidal was slightly more efficient than Omarion Hampton (18 yards) on the same number of carries. Vidal has seen more rotational offensive snaps over the Chargers' last three games, and over that span he has logged 20 carries for 103 yards and a touchdown and six catches (on nine targets) for 29 yards and a score. His role may continue to expand following the Week 7 bye, with the Chargers' next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Mitchell turned two carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned four kickoffs for 87 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Week 6 was the lowest usage Mitchell has seen this season, and his 17 snaps on offense were third most among Chargers running backs behind Omarion Hampton (34) and Kimani Vidal (25). Through six regular-season games, Mitchell has turned 35 carries into 139 yards and added 12 catches (on 15 targets) for 52 yards and a score, but it's hard to put much trust into any of the Chargers' skill-position players given the team's poor start to the season. Perhaps the Week 7 bye will help the Chargers right the ship, with their next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Johnston caught one of three targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Johnston needed just one catch to set a season high in receiving yards, but he was tackled at the 1-yard line to keep him without a touchdown this season after consecutive eight-touchdown regular seasons. The Chargers proceeded to back up 11 yards from there and settled for a field goal. Johnston has caught a deep pass in each of the past two games, securing a 44-yard catch in the Week 5 loss to Seattle prior to the 57-yard catch against the Chiefs. The 2023 first-round pick has just eight catches through five appearances heading into LA's Week 7 bye.

short_comment: Herbert completed 22 of 37 passes for 204 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed five times for 26 yards.
long_comment: Herbert continued to struggle but once again got little help from his teammates. Top wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) exited early, and the Chargers couldn't generate much on the ground, as Herbert led the team in rushing yards. Herbert was held without a touchdown for the first time this season after throwing exactly one touchdown pass in each of the previous five games. The 0-6 Chargers are the first team to six losses this season, as the Titans notched their first win of the season over the Colts on Sunday to improve to 1-5, while the winless Dolphins were on bye. Herbert will be on bye in Week 7 before his next opportunity to snap this season-opening losing streak in a nominal road game against the Rams in Week 8.

short_comment: Hampton rushed seven times for 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: The Chargers continued to deloy an ineffective backfield rotation, as Hampton got 11 touches compared to 10 for Kimani Vidal and two for Keaton Mitchell. None of the three running backs exceeded 3.0 yards per carry while QB Justin Herbert led the team with 26 rushing yards. Hampton has been trending in the wrong direction, with his rushing yardage dropping with each subsequent game since a 94-yard performance on the ground in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll look to reverse that trend in Week 8 against the Rams following a Week 7 bye.

short_comment: Henley (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
long_comment: Henley was listed as questionable for Sunday's game due to a knee injury. The linebacker was limited in practice all week due to the injury but has recovered enough to suit up for the Chargers' Sunday divisional contest against the Chiefs.

short_comment: The Chargers placed Ingold on injured reserve Thursday due to a shoulder injury.
long_comment: Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, Ingold wasn't included on the Chargers' initial Week 6 injury report Wednesday before being a late addition on account of the shoulder issue. He'll be sidelined for at least the next four games, making him ineligible to play until Week 11 versus the Jets on Nov. 22. The fullback hadn't logged any carries and recorded three receptions for 35 yards on four targets through Los Angeles' first five games.

short_comment: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Perryman (undisclosed) won't be reinstated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
long_comment: Per Ricardo Sandoval of USA Today, Harbaugh said back on Sept. 1 that he expected Perryman to spend the minimum four games on IR due to his unspecified injury, but the veteran linebacker will now be sidelined for a sixth straight game to begin the campaign. The 33-year-old appeared in 10 games for the Chargers in 2025, logging 47 tackles and three pass breakups.

short_comment: Curl logged four tackles (two solo) during the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
long_comment: Curl was on the field for all but one of the Rams' defensive snaps during Sunday's win. The veteran safety has logged four stops or fewer in five of seven regular-season games and is up to 34 tackles (20 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.

short_comment: Lake finished Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders with seven tackles (four solo).
long_comment: Lake ended up leading the Rams in tackles Sunday, and he's posted at least six stops in each of the first seven games of the regular season. The fifth-year defensive back is up to 49 tackles (32 solo), nine pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one forced fumble in 2026.

short_comment: Whittington wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: Even with Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Whittington played just 15 of 72 offensive snaps and ran only two routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks. Whittington currently profiles as nothing more than a special-teamer and blocker, keeping him far from fantasy relevance for the time being.

short_comment: Atwell wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: With Davante Adams (hamstring) out, Atwell was active and played 25 offensive snaps. He ran 20 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks, tying Konata Mumpfield for second on the team behind Puka Nacua's 31, but Atwell was just doing cardio out there. He's not a reliable fantasy target, even with Adams injured.

short_comment: Mumpfield caught one of two targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 35-21 win at Las Vegas.
long_comment: With Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR and Puka Nacua dealing with a calf injury going into game day, it looked like Mumpfield was going to see his role expand in Week 7. While he was second on the team in snaps (28) at wide receiver Sunday, Mumpfield still lagged far behind Nacua (58). As long as the latter remains available, Mumpfield appears unlikely to draw more than a few targets in any given game.

short_comment: Higbee caught two of three targets for 14 yards during Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: Higbee was expected to have a chance to see an increase in production with wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) unavailable, but the tight end put together a disappointing performance. Fellow tight ends Colby Parkinson (5-48-0) and Davis Allen (4-20-2) had more impressive days, and it may be hard to predict which of the three will be the go-to option any given week until Terrance Ferguson (ankle) returns from injured reserve.

short_comment: Stafford completed 23 of 29 passes for 195 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed three times for minus-3 yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
long_comment: Stafford was operating with a less-than-100-percent Puka Nacua (calf) and without Davante Adams (IR, hamstring), so his reduced passing yardage total wasn't entirely surprising. The reigning MVP still found a way to deliver a highly useful fantasy performance via a trio of first-half scoring strikes to Davis Allen (three, five yards) and Nacua (11 yards). Stafford also extended a streak of games with better than a 74.0 percent completion rate to three, and his 79.3 percent tally Sunday was a season-high figure. Stafford next takes aim at the Chargers defense in a Week 8 home matchup next Sunday.

short_comment: Corum rushed 17 times for 93 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for eight yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
long_comment: Corum led the Rams in rush attempts and was a close runner-up to Kyren Williams in rushing yards. Corum, like Williams, crossed the goal line as well, recording a four-yard touchdown run with 6:34 remaining in the fourth quarter. Corum's carry and yardage totals were also season highs, but given he'd logged single-digit rush attempts in each of the prior four games, he's more likely than not to continue operating in a clear complementary role behind Williams most weeks.

short_comment: Parkinson caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: With Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle) both out and injured for Los Angeles, Parkinson's six targets were second on the team behind Puka Nacua's 10. The tight end ran just 14 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks, but Los Angeles used multiple tight ends, led by Tyler Higbee's 18 routes. Parkinson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fringe TE1/2 headed into Week 8 against the Chargers.

short_comment: Allen caught four of five targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: With Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle) sidelined for the Rams, Allen was thrust into an elevated role on offense for Los Angeles. He ended up running just 12 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks but made the most of his chances, particularly in the red zone, where Allen caught three- and five-yard touchdowns in the first half. Allen's volume of routes isn't enough to make him a reliable fantasy option moving forward.

short_comment: Williams rushed 16 times for 99 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 22 yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
long_comment: Williams logged one fewer carry than Blake Corum but outgained his teammate by six yards, and although the former's lost fumble came at the Rams' 30-yard line, it didn't lead to any Raiders points. Williams scored his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a 17-yard run late in the first half, and he fell a yard short of his first 100-yard effort of the season. Despite the division of labor in a game that yielded a run-friendly game script, Williams should remain the clear leader of the ground attack in a Week 8 home matchup against the Chargers next Sunday.

short_comment: Nacua brought in eight of 10 targets for 68 yards and a touchdown and rushed twice for 10 yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
long_comment: Nacua led the Rams in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, playing through his calf injury without issue while also helping make up for the absence of Davante Adams (IR, hamstring). Nacua rounded out his busy day with his second touchdown catch of the season, which came from 11 yards out with just over four minutes remaining in the second quarter. Nacua figures to be even more involved than usual while Adams is sidelined, and he'll take a 45-485-2 line into a Week 8 home matchup against the Chargers next Sunday.

short_comment: McManus did not attempt a field goal and went 5-for-5 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
long_comment: McManus signed with Los Angeles this week after Blake Grupe (knee) was placed on injured reserve. The kicker wasn't tested much Sunday, but he was able to avoid making any mistakes. McManus may have a chance to attempt his first field goal as a member of the Rams in Week 8 against the Chargers.

short_comment: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The first-round rookie will not enter Sunday's contest unless both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

short_comment: The Rams elevated Kendricks from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
long_comment: It's the first time that Kendricks has been elevated to the Rams' active roster this season. He'll be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders and is expected to start at inside linebacker in replacement of the injured Nate Landman (concussion), per Nate Atkins of The Athletic. Kendricks spent the last few weeks of the 2025 campaign with the 49ers and appeared in three regular-season games, logging six tackles (three solo) in that span.

short_comment: Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Garrett (knee) could have his 21-day practice window opened next week, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: The Rams are in shambles from an injury standpoint headed into Sunday's game against the Raiders, but help may be on the horizon in the form of Garrett. The All-Pro edge rusher hasn't played since Week 1 in Australia.

short_comment: The Rams placed Turner (groin) on injured reserve Wednesday.
long_comment: Turner suffered a significant groin injury during the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, and the health issue is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest that Turner can return is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. In his absence, Braden Fiske should move into a starting role on the defensive line opposite Aaron Donald, while Tyler Davis and Larrell Murchison work in rotation.

short_comment: The Rams placed Ford (triceps) on injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: The move is an expected one, given that Ford suffered a season-ending triceps injury during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday. The veteran defensive tackle will shift his focus toward rehab and being fully healthy for the 2027 season, which is the final year of his three-year, $27.6 million contract with the Rams.

short_comment: Ferguson (ankle), who is eligible to come off injured reserve next week, isn't expected to be ready at that time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Ferguson, who was placed on injured reserve in advance of Week 4 action, will be eligible to return in Week 8 against the Chargers. However, it appears as though the tight end's return isn't imminent, with Schefter's report suggesting that Ferguson's recovery "will take some time." In his absence, Tyler Higbee profiles as the Rams' main pass-catching TE, with Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen also mixing in.

short_comment: Rodriguez tallied four tackles (one solo) during Miami's win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Rodriguez had his worst outing of an otherwise impressive rookie campaign, as he compiled a season-low four tackles. The 24-year-old has recorded 61 tackles (26 solo) across his first six outings and will look to bounce back during next week's matchup against the Patriots.

short_comment: Brooks posted nine tackles (five solo) during the Dolphins' win Sunday over the Jets.
long_comment: Brooks was productive against the Jets, leading Miami in tackles and helping the team win their first game of the campaign. The 29-year-old has had a solid start to the season, compiling eight or more tackles in five of his first six appearances. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup versus the Patriots.
