short_comment: Kacmarek played 29 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps but did not appear in the box score in the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Kacmarek played 45 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps. The No. 2 tight end's blocking role was in stark contrast to position mate Greg Dulcich's team-leading target share, and the  two players are expected to continue filling similar roles for the foreseeable future.

short_comment: Coleman did not catch his only target in the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Coleman played 10 offensive snaps in Sunday's win. The fifth-round rookie participated in just 15 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays, taking a back seat to third-round rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas.

short_comment: Bell caught three of his four targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: The third-round rookie played 31 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. Bell was in on 48 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays and saw the second-most targets behind tight end Greg Dulcich (five).

short_comment: Allen logged six snaps on special teams and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Allen -- who was claimed off waivers by the Dolphins one day after being let go by the Commanders on Oct. 8 -- was cleared to make his debut with his new team Sunday. He was limited to work on special teams, but he could carve himself a role on offense as he gets more familiar with the playbook. Jaylen Wright left Sunday's game and did not return due to a quadriceps injury, and if he cannot play against the Raiders in Week 8, then Allen will step into the RB2 role behind Ollie Gordon.

short_comment: Gonzalez reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
long_comment: Gonzalez was perfect in the Dolphins' first regular-season win in 2026. The kicker made all four of his PATs on Sunday against the Jets and is set to be elevated to the active roster again for the team's Week 8 game versus the Patriots.

short_comment: Washington caught all three targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets. He rushed two times for eight yards.
long_comment: Greg Dulcich ended up leading the Dolphins in targets (five), catches (five) and yards (86) on a day Malik Willis attempted just 21 passes and spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers. Washington will look to bounce back next Sunday against the Patriots, where he'll have some WR4 appeal in fantasy.

short_comment: Dulcich caught all five of his targets for 86 yards in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Dulcich led the Dolphins in catches, receiving yards and targets as Miami notched its first win of the season. The 2022 third-round pick of the Broncos is still searching for his first touchdown of the season after scoring once in 10 games for the Dolphins in 2025. Dulcich is likely to remain a key target for Malik Willis in Week 8 against the Patriots.

short_comment: Douglas (ankle) caught two of three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Douglas made an immediate impact in his first action since Week 2. The rookie third-round pick capped the game's first drive with a seven-yard touchdown catch for his first NFL TD, then stayed in along the sideline to score again on a 63-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter. Miami utilizes a run-heavy approach when possible, but the Dolphins may be forced to throw more if they fall behind as expected in Week 8 against the Patriots, which could lead to more opportunities for Douglas.

short_comment: Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns while rushing six times for 39 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Willis gave the Dolphins their first lead of the season with a seven-yard touchdown pass to Caleb Douglas on the opening drive. After the Jets tied the game on the ensuing possession, Miami reclaimed the lead with a one-yard Ollie Gordon touchdown run, and Willis extended the advantage to 14 points with a two-yard touchdown run in the waning seconds of the first half. Miami's offense stalled for most of the second half until Willis found Douglas for a 63-yard catch and run to take a 28-17 lead with 4:44 remaining in the fourth quarter. The Jets scored on their next drive, but Willis sealed his first win as Miami's QB with a successful fourth-down QB sneak to pick up a first down and set up victory formation. Up next for Willis and the 1-5 Dolphins is a Week 8 home game against the Patriots.

short_comment: Gordon rushed 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown while catching one of three targets for no gain in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Gordon extended his touchdown streak to four games with a one-yard rushing score in the first quarter. Over that four-game span, Gordon has 69 carries for 332 yards and four touchdowns, having established himself as the go-to option in Miami's backfield following De'Von Achane's season-ending ACL tear. If the 1-5 Dolphins can stay competitive at home against the Patriots in Week 8, Gordon would be in line to handle another heavy rushing workload, especially if Jaylen Wright (quadriceps) doesn't play after exiting Sunday's win.

short_comment: Wright (quadriceps) left Sunday's game against the Jets and did not return to the contest.
long_comment: Wright exited Miami's victory late in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. Wright filled a clear complementary role behind Ollie Gordon, and the former's health will be worth monitoring during Week 8 prep ahead of a home matchup against the Patriots next Sunday.

short_comment: Trader (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's game against the Jets, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Trader exited Sunday's contest in the third quarter with a shoulder injury. The starting strong safety has been thoroughly vetted and deemed healthy enough to return to the Dolphins' divisional showdown with the Jets.

short_comment: The Dolphins activated Louis (knee) from injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Louis returned to practice Wednesday when the Dolphins opened his 21-day window. The safety is set to play in Sunday's divisional bout with the Jets after missing the last four games due to a knee injury he sustained in Week 1 against the Raiders.

short_comment: Savaiinaea (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Savaiinaea injured his ankle during the Dolphins' Week 5 loss to the Bengals. The second-year offensive lineman had extra time to recover thanks to the Week 6 bye, and given his ability to practice in full Wednesday, Savaiinaea should start at right guard against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Cashman recorded 12 tackles (8 solo) including 2.0 sacks and four passes defensed during Sunday's 16-10 win versus the Colts.
long_comment: On a day where Minnesota held Indianapolis' offense almost completely in check, Cashman arguably shined brighter than any other player on his unit. It was the first time he's ever logged two sacks in a single game, and his four pass breakups marked another career high. He profiles as a strong IDP option in most formats going into a Week 8 matchup at Detroit.

short_comment: Smith recorded four tackles (two solo) including 0.5 sacks and an interception during Sunday's 16-10 win versus the Colts.
long_comment: Smith sealed Minnesota's victory in Week 7 when he cut off a Daniel Jones pass intended for tight end Will Mallory with less than two minutes remaining in regulation. It was his first interception of the season, and the 40th of his illustrious career with the Vikings. He projects to play a rotational role again in Week 8 at Detroit.

short_comment: The left knee injury that forced Jones out of Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts isn't considered significant, and the running back is viewed as day-to-day, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: Jordan Mason (thumb) returned from injured reserve and stepped back in as the Vikings' lead ball carrier while Jones shifted into a change-of-pace role. Jones carried eight times for 26 yards and added one reception for no gain across 15 snaps before exiting with 12:22 remaining in the fourth quarter. After the game, head coach Kevin O'Connell acknowledged that Jones experienced an aggravation of the MCL sprain he previously sustained in Week 2. Jones was able to return to action the following week, but the results of an MRI on Monday will help determine whether he can avoid an absence during the Vikings' Week 8 game in Detroit.

short_comment: Jennings caught two of three targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
long_comment: The veteran wideout entered Week 7 with just two catches for nine yards across four games, so this counts as a breakout game for Jennings. He's running plenty of routes alongside Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison at receiver, but Jennings is deep down the list for targets in Minnesota. He's not a recommended fantasy play for next Sunday against the Lions' leaky secondary.

short_comment: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
long_comment: The veteran tight end scored Minnesota's only TD of the afternoon, connecting with Kyler Murray on a five-yard score early in the fourth quarter. Hockenson has seen more than five targets just once in six contests this season, and he'll take a 27-237-2 line on 32 targets into a potential revenge game in Week 8 against the Lions.

short_comment: Addison caught two of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts. He added three yards on his lone carry.
long_comment: No Viking caught more than four passes on the afternoon, and Justin Jefferson was the only member of the team to see more than five targets, so Addison's poor numbers were more a result of his offense's struggles overall than his own performance. The fourth-year wideout still has only one big game in his five appearances so far, with 90 of his 183 receiving yards and his only TD coming Week 3 against Tampa Bay. Addison will try to break out in Week 8 against a struggling Lions secondary.

short_comment: Mason carried the ball 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts. He failed to catch either of his two targets.
long_comment: Making his return from an IR stint due to a thumb injury that had kept him out since Week 1, Mason ended up leading the Vikings in rushing yards after Aaron Jones aggravated a knee injury and spotted in and out of the lineup. Jones had been getting a hefty workload while Mason was sidelined, but their roles could be reversed in Week 8 against the Lions.

short_comment: Murray completed 14 of 24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts. He added 39 rushing yards on five carries.
long_comment: With the Vikings' defense dominating on their side of the ball, Murray's modest numbers were enough to keep the team undefeated. He did shine on a fourth-quarter drive that produced Minnesota's only TD. scrambling for a 35-yard gain to get the ball into the red zone and then finding T.J. Hockenson for a five-yard score. Murray has just a 3:2 TD:INT through five starts and has yet to add a touchdown on the ground, but he could put together his first big performance of the season in a Week 8 clash with the Lions.

short_comment: Jefferson caught four of seven targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
long_comment: The targets and receiving yards actually led the Vikings in a low-scoring defensive battle, but it was T.J. Hockenson on the other end of Kyler Murray's only TD pass. Jefferson is still looking for his first 100-yard performance of the season, and he's been held under 60 yards in three of his five games. The star wideout could be poised to finally break out in Week 8 against the Lions' struggling secondary.

short_comment: Reichard went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
long_comment: Reichard was unable to remain perfect Sunday, but he did deliver at least three field goals for the fifth straight game. The kicker converted kicks from 28 and 47 yards in the first half before later adding a 52-yard make with 1:39 left in regulation, giving Minnesota a 16-10 lead. Reichard's first miss of the season came in the fourth quarter when Grover Stewart got a paw on the kicker's 59-yard try. Reichard is out to a remarkable start to the season, going 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including six makes from 50-plus yards, over six contests so far.

short_comment: Price (head) was back on the field for the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Colts, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
long_comment: Price was being evaluated by medical staff for a possible concussion, but he's been cleared to return to Sunday's contest. He'll see most of his playing time as a returner on special teams while operating in a rotational role on offense.

short_comment: Darrisaw (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
long_comment: Darrisaw has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest. The starting left tackle will protect Kyler Murray as the Vikings attempt to maintain a perfect record through Week 7.

short_comment: Jurgens (elbow) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
long_comment: Jurgens was activated from IR on Saturday. The offensive lineman has recovered from his elbow injury and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game.

short_comment: Yurosek (ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
long_comment: Yurosek was activated from the Vikings' injured reserve Saturday, just in time for Week 5. The 24-year-old has yet to play in the 2026 season. He is expected to add depth behind T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew versus the Saints.

short_comment: Thorson (hamstring) was a full participant in practice Wednesday and Thursday.
long_comment: Thorson missed Sunday's Week 4 win over Miami due to his hamstring injury. However, with a pair of full practices to begin Week 5 prep, he's probably good to go for Week 5 versus New Orleans. Thorson should thus reclaim his role as the Vikings' punter.

short_comment: Jackson (knee) was placed on injured reserve by the Vikings on Tuesday.
long_comment: Jackson suffered a torn meniscus during Sunday's 15-10 win over Miami, and he was already set to miss the rest of the regular season, so Tuesday's move to the IR comes as no surprise. Joe Huber is the top candidate to take over as Minnesota's starting left guard in Jackson's absence.

short_comment: Metellus recorded nine tackles (four solo), including 0.5 sacks, and a defensed pass Sunday against Tampa Bay in a 23-16 victory.
long_comment: Metellus logged the second-most tackles on Minnesota behind Eric Wilson (11). One of his stops was an assisted sack of Baker Mayfield on the first play of the fourth quarter. Metellus has played every defensive snap for the Vikings so far this season and has racked up 20 tackles and two pass defenses through three contests.

short_comment: Jones registered nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, and returned one punt for 19 yards in Thursday's loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Jones finished second on New England in stops behind Christian Elliss (13). He also notched his first sack of the campaign, bringing down Caleb Williams on a second-down play near the end of the first half, though Chicago scored a touchdown on its following snap. Jones is off to a strong start to the campaign, recording 36 tackles (including 1.0 sacks) and five defensed passes (including an interception) through seven contests.

short_comment: Elliss tallied 13 tackles (eight solo) in a Week 7 loss to Chicago on Thursday.
long_comment: Elliss's 13 stops not only led New England, they also tied a career-best mark. The veteran linebacker logged a 100 percent defensive snap share for the fourth time this season and posted his second double-digit tackle performance. Elliss set a career best with 94 regular-season stops over 15 games last season, and he's on pace to easily surpass that mark with 51 tackles (including 1.0 sacks) through seven contests in 2026.

short_comment: Williams returned two kickoffs for 47 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: It was the second game in a row in which Williams saw one target from Drake Maye, and the second-year pro's 21 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Patriots wide receivers. He's been surpassed by Efton Chism in the passing game, and with A.J. Brown back in the mix, it seems like most of Williams' impact moving forward will be on kickoffs as a returner. His playing time will take an even greater hit upon the returns of Mack Hollins (calf) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) from injured reserve. The Patriots will stay on the road for Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Kiner rushed four times for 13 yards in Thursday's Week 7 loss to Chicago. He also returned four kickoffs for 102 yards.
long_comment: Kiner came into Thursday having gained 50-plus rushing yards in consecutive contests, but he was much less impactful versus the Bears. Part of that was due to New England playing from behind and tallying just 17 total carries as a team (to 31 pass attempts), but it's also notable that Kiner logged just six offensive snaps, well behind Rhamondre Stevenson's 37 and less than half of TreyVeon Henderson's 13. While Kiner's previous two performances gave him a little momentum in fantasy, he's unlikely to be a reliable asset while Stevenson and Henderson are healthy.

short_comment: Raridon caught three of four targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's Week 7 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Raridon got open late in the third quarter and hauled in a nicely placed pass from Drake Maye for a 30-yard score. The rookie tight end finished third on the team with 56 receiving yards and tied for third with three receptions. Raridon is clearly behind Hunter Henry, who posted a 7-71-0 receiving line on seven targets, in the tight-end pecking order, but he's shown promise early in his career with 12 catches on 16 targets for 168 yards and two TDs through six games.

short_comment: Chism caught his sole target for 16 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: Chism saw the third most offensive snaps at wide receiver for the Patriots behind A.J. Brown's 49 and DeMario Douglas' 35. The 24-year-old was not given as much attention as in the prior two weeks, with his target share dropping from four targets in Week 5 and six targets in Week 6 to just one in Week 7.

short_comment: Douglas caught three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: Douglas played 35 of the Patriots' 54 offensive snaps in the contest and did not find the end zone. The wide receiver had logged three touchdowns in the prior two contests but has now returned to a role with lower priority as A.J. Brown becomes reacquainted with the offense.

short_comment: Henderson rushed three times for nine yards and secured both targets for 14 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: Henderson's modest numbers underscore how modest a role he filled in the high-scoring loss. Rhamondre Stevenson had just six carries in his own right, but he also recorded a team-high 93 receiving yards on five catches. Henderson's rush attempts and rushing yards were both season lows, and the second-year back will look to bounce back in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Henry secured all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: The veteran tight end was a key contributor throughout the night, finishing with team-high figures in receptions and targets while ending second in receiving yards. All three components of Henry's receiving line also were season-high figures, and he now has between 44 and 71 receiving yards in four consecutive games. Henry will take a 26-296-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Borregales made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three extra-point tries Thursday in a Week 7 loss to the Bears.
long_comment: Borregales was limited to extra-point tries until the Patriots' final drive of the game, when the kicker nailed a 47-yard field goal with less than a minute remaining to bring his team to within six points ahead of an unsuccessful onside kick. The second-year pro has been held to just four FG attempts -- all of which he has made -- over his past four contests after going 5-for-7 across New England's first three games of the season. The lower volume is largely due to the Patriots' improvement on offense over that four-game stretch, as Borregales has gone 14-for-15 on point-after attempts during that span.

short_comment: Brown brought in three of six targets for 48 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: Brown entered the night looking to put a fairly forgettable Week 6 return from injury behind him, but the veteran wideout could only slightly improve his numbers in the high-scoring loss. He was fairly quiet until the second half, when he had 16- and 14-yard grabs. Brown did finish second in targets on the night for New England, but Drake Maye focused most on tight end Hunter Henry and running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who saw a combined 12 targets. With Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder) out for at least three more games, Brown will have a chance to see elevated volume in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards and brought in all five targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: Stevenson had another tough day on the ground, especially considering he gained 13 of his 22 yards on one carry. However, the veteran back had a standout performance as a receiver, leading the Patriots in receiving yards on the night with a big hand from a weaving 48-yard touchdown catch off an end-of-half screen play. Stevenson is now averaging just 3.7 yards per carry across the first seven games of the campaign, but he's up to a 20-204-1 receiving line on 24 targets heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding four rushes for 26 yards and another score in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
long_comment: Maye's final line was one that could have easily been generated in victory, but the 2024 first-round pick couldn't quite help the Patriots keep pace with the high-powered Bears offense. Nevertheless, he was able to post his second 300-yard effort in the last three games, while also tossing multiple touchdowns for the fourth straight contest. Maye connected with Rhamondre Stevenson and Eli Raridon from 48 and 30 yards, respectively, for those two scoring strikes, the former coming off a screen pass on the last snap of the first half. Those big plays were preceded by Maye's seven-yard scoring run early in the second quarter, and he also pulled his season completion rate up to 65.9 percent with Thursday's highly efficient effort. The third-year signal-caller should have a good opportunity to stay hot in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve by the Patriots on Thursday.
long_comment: Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Jets, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Walter Rouse will take over as the team's starting left tackle Thursday night versus the Bears.

short_comment: Moses (foot) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
long_comment: Moses was forced out of the Patriots' contest in Week 6 versus the Jets due to a foot injury after just nine snaps, and he was seen wearing a walking boot after that game. Now, despite a short turnaround and having been limited at practice all week, he's in line to play Thursday. He should start at right tackle in Week 7.

short_comment: Woodson (shoulder) is officially active for Thursday's game against the Bears.
long_comment: Woodson has been nursing a nagging shoulder issue since picking it up back in Week 2 versus the Steelers, but he'll tough it out for the fourth straight contest in Week 7. He projects to start at safety next to veteran Kevin Byard on Thursday.

short_comment: Byard (chest) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
long_comment: Byard dealt with a minor chest issue during the week that stuck him with a 'questionable' tag Wednesday, but as expected, he'll be available for Week 7. He figures to play a near-every down role against a run-heavy Chicago offense.

short_comment: Gonzalez (illness) is listed as active for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
long_comment: Gonzalez was a late addition to the Patriots' injury report ahead of Thursday's kickoff, but he subsequently participated in warmups and is in line to be able to play through his illness after all. In four games thus far, the star cornerback, who anchors New England's secondary, has recorded 14 tackles and five passes defended.

short_comment: Bryant (ankle) was a full participant at the Patriots' practice Tuesday.
long_comment: Bryant has opened the week with back-to-back full sessions with the Patriots, and he may be trending toward a return to action in the near future. The offensive lineman has missed the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point after picking up an ankle injury during the preseason, but the team opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday. With New England traveling to face the Bears on Thursday, Bryant may not be ready to go in advance of Week 7, but Wednesday's injury report will provide more clarity toward his status.

short_comment: Granderson totaled four tackles, including 1.5 sacks, in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Granderson helped keep the game close with a pair of key sacks. He brought down Aaron Rodgers near the end of the second quarter to help hold the Steelers to a field goal, then split a sack in the red zone at the end of the third period to again limit Pittsburgh to three points. Granderson is up to 5.5 sacks through six games on the campaign, giving him an excellent chance of surpassing the career-high mark of 8.5 sacks he established over 17 contests in 2023.

short_comment: Werner finished Sunday's loss to the Steelers with eight tackles (three solo).
long_comment: Werner had a two-game streak of double-digit stops snapped, but he was still plenty productive. The veteran linebacker dealt with a neck injury in early October but appears past that issue, as he's played every Saints defensive snap in three straight contests. Werner leads New Orleans with 54 tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through seven games.

short_comment: Sanker posted nine tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Sanker recorded his second-highest tackle tally of the campaign to lead New Orleans in that category. The second-year defender has now tallied six or more stops in five of his seven games this season. With 44 tackles through seven contests, Sanker is easily on pace to surpass the 80 stops he notched in 17 games as a rookie.

short_comment: Fant gathered in all two targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 16-10 defeat against Pittsburgh.
long_comment: After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.

short_comment: Lance reeled in all two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone. The 24-year-old has logged 332 offensive snaps this season, third in the receiving corps behind Chris Olave (387) and Devaughn Vele (438). However, despite being on the field more often than most of the other wideouts on the roster, Lance hasn't been productive thus far in his rookie campaign.

short_comment: Miller rushed eight times for six yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers in Paris.
long_comment: The Saints got absolutely nothing going on the ground against Pittsburgh, rushing 17 times for 18 yards as a team, so it's not like Miller and his team-leading eight carries was the only issue. New Orleans heads into its bye in Week 8, and Travis Etienne (hamstring) will be eligible to come off injured reserve for Week 9 against the Browns. When both Etienne and Alvin Kamara were healthy and active together earlier this season, Miller was a healthy inactive.

short_comment: Brown hauled in all three targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
long_comment: Brown had the most productive game of his NFL career thus far, catching more passes than he had in his previous five appearances combined. The 2026 No. 190 overall pick should continue to get consistent work on special teams. However, despite the recent uptick in offensive snaps, it's unknown if Brown will continue to be more involved as a pass catcher moving forward.

short_comment: Johnson caught one of three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
long_comment: Johnson was held in check yet again in Week 7. The tight end has now gone three straight games without exceeding 16 receiving yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3. Johnson has slowly become an unreliable fantasy option as the season has progressed, but he'll have the opportunity to hit the reset button during the Saints' bye week in Week 8.

short_comment: Vele caught all five of his targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
long_comment: The third-year wideout was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD pass of the day, hauling in a one-yard toss in the second quarter for the Saints' final points. Vele tied his career high with his third touchdown of the season, and his 33-348-3 line on 48 targets through seven games has him tracking toward a career-best campaign heading into a Week 8 bye. His role could shrink significantly after the bye, however, if rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to make his NFL debut.

short_comment: Kamara carried the ball six times for five yards and caught all seven of his targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
long_comment: The Saints' ground game was completely shut down, as quarterback Tyler Shough led the team with a mere seven rushing yards, but Kamara still contributed through the air and led New Orleans in catches while tying Barion Brown for the game high in receiving yards. Since missing the season opener, Kamara has put together 258 scrimmage yards and three total TDs (two rushing, one receiving) over six games, but the backfield could get more crowded after a Week 8 bye if Travis Etienne (hamstring) is cleared to return.

short_comment: Carlson went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his lone extra-point try during Sundays' 16-10 loss to the Steelers in Paris.
long_comment: Carlson connected on a 38-yard field goal early in the second quarter, but his 52-yarder in the fourth missed wide right and gave the Steelers the ball back with good field position. He's missed one kick in each of his last five games, and head coach Kellen Moore told reporters after Sunday's contest that "it's fair to evaluate" Carlson's kicking issues to open the season, per Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com. The Saints will be on a bye for Week 8, so the team could bring in another kicker to compete with Carlson before their next game in Week 9 against the Browns on Sunday, Nov. 8.

short_comment: Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers. He added seven rushing yards on three carries.
long_comment: With the Saints' ground game getting absolutely nowhere -- Shough actually led the team in rushing yards -- the second-year QB had to air it out frequently once again, but the volume didn't result in much production. Shough will head into a Week 8 bye averaging 39 pass attempts a game -- the fourth-highest mark in the league behind Matthew Stafford, Dak Prescott and Bryce Young -- to go along with a 13:6 TD:INT and 1,721 passing yards.

short_comment: Olave caught six of 10 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
long_comment: While Olave saw a team-high 10 targets, Alvin Kamara caught one more pass and gained one more receiving yard for the team leads in those categories, while Devaughn Vele caught Tyler Shough's only TD. Olave has failed to reach 60 yards in three straight games after topping 100 in three of his first four contests this season, but he'll get a bye week to reset before facing the Browns in Week 9.

short_comment: Reid (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris.
long_comment: Reid sustained a concussion in Sunday's international game and will not return to the contest. The safety has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist for every step of his return journey.

short_comment: Donaldson (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris.
long_comment: Donaldson picked up the injury during the first quarter and has been taken to the locker room to undergo more tests on his shoulder injury. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller would be the remaining healthy running backs on the Saints active roster for the rest of Sunday's game if Donaldson is not cleared to return.

short_comment: Rattler is active and will remain the Saints' No. 2 quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
long_comment: Rattler was able to beat out Zach Wilson for the top backup job behind Tyler Shough during the preseason and has maintained his positioning on the depth chart all season. For the seventh week in a row, Wilson will be inactive as the Saints' emergency No. 3 signal-caller.

short_comment: Jennings (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
long_comment: Jennings will play in his first contest since sustaining a knee injury in the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders. The linebacker should work back into the edge rotation behind starters Chase Young and Carl Granderson.

short_comment: Elliss (calf) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers.
long_comment: Elliss was limited earlier in the practice week and will return to the lineup after missing the previous three games. The 31-year-old linebacker has recorded 24 tackles (11 solo) and one pass breakup across three starts this season.

short_comment: Reese posted seven tackles (five solo), including 0.5 sacks, in Sunday's 27-21 overtime victory against the Texans.
long_comment: Reese continues to produce nice tackle numbers, as he's recorded seven or more stops in five of his seven games this season. The rookie out of Ohio State didn't notch a sack in his first four contests, but he's starting to pick up the pace with 1.5 sacks across his past three games. Reese has logged 100 percent of New York's defensive snaps in all but one of his appearances so far.

short_comment: McFadden notched 10 tackles (all solo) in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win against the Texans.
long_comment: Among McFadden's 10 stops were two tackles for loss. The veteran linebacker had logged only three defensive snaps while serving primarily on special teams before Sunday, but he stepped into a starting role and played every one of the Giants' defensive snaps against Houston. It appears McFadden is going to be the replacement for inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, who landed on IR due to a chest injury last week.

short_comment: The Giants signed Desrosiers off the Chargers' practice squad Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
long_comment: With Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) now on injured reserve, the Giants bolstered the roster by adding Desrosiers. The undrafted rookie appeared in three preseason games for the Chargers, amassing 166 yards and one touchdown off 23 carries. While Desrosiers is listed behind Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Devin Singletary on the depth chart, he could see action if one of those players gets injured.

short_comment: The Giants placed Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.

short_comment: Mooney caught one of three targets for four yards and rushed once for three yards during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win against the Texans.
long_comment: Mooney has now been held to one or no catches in three of the past four games, and he has yet to exceed two receptions in a contest this season. The wide receiver will continue to be an unattractive fantasy option when the Giants return to action Week 9 against the Eagles.

short_comment: Winston turned four carries into four yards and a touchdown during the Giants' 27-21 overtime win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy to serve as the starting quarterback for Week 7 after Winston filled in that role in each of the four prior games. McCarthy looked more poised in the pocket, but all four of the Giants' touchdowns came on the ground, with Winston finding the end zone on a designed QB sneak late in the second quarter. That figures to be the veteran's role moving forward unless McCarthy misses time.

short_comment: Head coach John Harbaugh reiterated Monday that he's confident in Zvada and said that the Giants have no plans to work out other kickers, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
long_comment: Though the Giants escaped with a 27-21 overtime win over the Texans on Sunday, Zvada had his second rough performance in the past three weeks. The undrafted rookie out of Michigan was unable to connect on field-goal tries of 44 and 56 yards, giving him five misses on 18 attempts through seven games. The Giants are hoping that their upcoming Week 8 bye will give Zvada some time to iron out kinks and refine his approach before the team returns to action Nov. 8 versus the Eagles.

short_comment: Skattebo is expected to "OK" after tweaking his hamstring on a 42-yard run in overtime during Sunday's 27-21 win over the Texans, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: Skattebo's explosive run put the Giants within field-goal range before he was subbed out for Devin Singletary, who ran up the middle for a 30-yard score to seal the win on the very next play. Though he told Dan Graziano of ESPN.com after the game that he "felt something" in his hamstring that prompted him to slide down at the end of his run rather than being tackled to the ground, Skattebo doesn't sound like he'll require an MRI and should be ready to play in the Giants' next game Nov. 8 versus the Eagles following a Week 8 bye. After being limited to just six snaps in a Week 6 loss to the Saints following a string of poor outings to begin the campaign, Skattebo stepped back into a lead role out of the backfield in Sunday's victory and delivered his best performance of the season, finishing with 121 total yards and a touchdown on 18 touches.

short_comment: Likely caught two of four targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans.
long_comment: With J.J. McCarthy inserted under center for his first start with the Giants, Likely took a big hit in production, as Malik Nabers led the team in targets (nine), catches (seven) and yards (111) despite the tough on-paper matchup with cornerback Derek Stingley. Likely will try to get back on track coming out of the Week 8 bye when the Giants face the Eagles on the road in Week 9.

short_comment: Fields caught four of five targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over Houston.
long_comment: In J.J. McCarthy's first start of the season, Fields had his best performance as a pro, capping his day with a 47-yard catch-and-run in the first quarter. The rookie wideout set a new career high in both receiving yards and catches after hauling in exactly two passes in each of his first six games for the Giants. Fields will head into the Giants' bye with a 16-248-1 line on 30 targets before facing the Eagles in Week 9.

short_comment: Singletary carried the ball five times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught all three of his targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 27-24 overtime win over the Texans.
long_comment: Attrition may have helped solve the Giants' backfield mess, at least in the short term. Tyrone Tracy left the game in the second quarter with a hamstring injury and didn't return, and Cam Skattebo may also have picked up a hamstring strain on his final tote of the day, a 42-yard dash in OT that set up a 30-yard TD run for Singletary that won the game. A well-timed Week 8 bye could allow both RBs to avoid missing any further time, but if either or both are still on the shelf on the other side of the break, Singletary could wind up handling a much bigger role in Week 9 against the Eagles.

short_comment: McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He added one yard on his only carry.
long_comment: Making his first start of the season, McCarthy was efficient in getting the Giants into position to score, but all four of their touchdowns came on the ground -- including a one-yard plunge by the man he replaced under center, Jameis Winston, in the second quarter. The victory alone was enough to keep McCarthy in the starting job, and after a bye he'll gear up for a Week 9 clash with the Eagles.

short_comment: Nabers caught seven of nine targets for 111 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans.
long_comment: The switch from Jameis Winston to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback for the Giants hasn't slowed Nabers down at all, and the team's No. 1 wideout extended his streak of games with over 100 receiving yards to four. During that surge, Nabers has delivered a 36-509-2 line on 51 targets, as he puts his injury-marred sophomore NFL campaign firmly behind him. He'll try to not to lose his momentum during the bye before facing the Eagles in Week 9.

short_comment: Eluemunor (calf) is active Week 7 against the Texans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
long_comment: Eluemunor managed just a pair of limited practices this week, but the veteran tackle will ultimately be available for a Giants team that has both Marcus Mbow (knee) and Josh Sills (coach's decision) on the inactive list Sunday.

short_comment: Nubin (neck) is active Week 7 against the Texans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
long_comment: After missing Week 6, Nubin will retake the field against Houston following a week of limited practices. Presumably in line to start, Nubin has recorded three or more combined tackles in each of the four games he has appeared in this year.

short_comment: Adebo (knee) is active Week 7 against the Texans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
long_comment: Adebo was activated from IR this week but still had a questionable tag after a week of limited practices. He'll ultimately get the nod to play for the first time since Week 1, and the veteran corner stands to see a significant number of snaps due to Greg Newsome (concussion) getting ruled out, plus several other members of the New York secondary are on IR.

short_comment: Edmunds (chest) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Edmunds will miss the rest of the 2026 season due to a torn chest muscle, so his placement on injured reserve opens up a spot on the Giants' 53-man roster. Micah McFadden is expected to start at inside linebacker alongside Arvell Reese for the rest of the season in Edmunds' absence, with Jack Kelly and Zaire Barnes providing depth at the position.

short_comment: Thomas (groin) does not have an injury designation against the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Thomas ended Week 7 prep with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He's been working through a groin injury the last few weeks but hasn't missed a game this season.

short_comment: Davis finished Sunday's Week 7 loss to Miami with three tackles (two solo) and one defensed pass.
long_comment: Davis' tackle tally was his lowest of the campaign, but he did record his first effort of multiple defensed passes. The durable linebacker has played every defensive snap for the Jets so far this season. With 46 stops through seven games, Davis is on pace for a 10th consecutive 100-tackle campaign.

short_comment: Sherwood totaled eight tackles (four solo) and two defensed passes Sunday in a loss to Miami.
long_comment: Of Sherwood's eight stops, two went for a loss. He also notched multiple defensed passes for the first time this season. Sherwood has been quite disruptive so far in 2026, tallying 54 tackles, four defensed passes, two forced fumbles and a recovered fumble through seven games.

short_comment: Belton registered nine tackles (six solo) in Sunday's loss to the Dolphins.
long_comment: Belton continues to put together a productive season, as he's posted seven or more stops in each of his past five games. The former New York Giant has yet to miss a defensive snap this season in his first campaign as a Jet. After posting a career-high 120 stops across 17 regular-season contests last year, Belton is on pace to challenge that mark with 56 tackles (including 1.0 sacks) through seven games this year. He's also tallied three defensed passes.

short_comment: Fitzpatrick posted 10 tackles (six solo) Sunday in a loss to Miami.

After missing Weeks 2 and 3 due to a groin injury, Fitzpatrick has logged every Jets defensive snap in four straight games as a stalwart of the team's secondary. The veteran safety has tallied 36 tackles and two defensed passes, including one interception, through five games during his first season with New York.

short_comment: Patrick did not garner a target during Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
long_comment: Patrick was on the field for just six offensive snaps in Week 7, and he went without a catch for the first time in three games so far this year. With Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper and Adonai Mitchell all available at wide receiver, it appears like Patrick doesn't have much of a role on offense at the moment.

short_comment: Mitchell failed to haul in any of his three targets during the Jets' 28-25 loss to the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: Mitchell was cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a finger injury. However, the third-year pro was unable to connect with Geno Smith during Sunday's loss, and Mitchell's 26 offensive snaps were third most among Jets wide receivers behind Garrett Wilson (50) and rookie Omar Cooper (38). Mitchell logged 15 targets through the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, but his offensive opportunities figure to be limited while competing for targets against Wilson, Cooper and tight ends Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq. The Jets will stay home for Week 8 against the Raiders, whose defense has given up the second-most passing touchdowns (16) this season.

short_comment: Davis logged a five-yard carry and caught all three of his targets for 49 yards during Sunday's 28-25 loss to Miami. He also added a tackle on special teams.
long_comment: Davis was on the field for 25 snaps (13 on offense, 12 on special teams) during Sunday's loss. He was barely used offensively until late in the fourth quarter, when he rattled off catches of two, 41 and six yards on consecutive plays, with the drive ending on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Geno Smith to Mason Taylor. Davis has operated as the Jets' RB2 behind Braelon Allen for the Jets' last four games, but the former's role will shrink considerably if Breece Hall (quadriceps) is cleared to return for Week 8 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 1.

short_comment: Sadiq caught his lone target for six yards in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
long_comment: With Mason Taylor dominating the targets at tight end for the Jets, Sadiq continues to fade into the background for an offense that is unable to support more than a couple pass catchers in the box score each week. Sadiq has just four catches for 21 yards over the last three weeks with Taylor back in the lineup.

short_comment: Sanders went 1-for-2 on field-goal tries and made both of his extra-point attempts during Sunday's 28-25 loss to Miami.
long_comment: Sanders hit the right upright on his first field-goal attempt of the day in the third quarter, missing his first kick since Week 1. The kicker later added a 33-yard make in the fourth quarter, but his earlier miss would prove to be the difference in the loss. Sanders has now gone 13-for-15 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, over the first seven games of the 2026 season.

short_comment: Taylor caught all five of his targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns while adding a two-point conversion in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
long_comment: Taylor bookended the scoring for the Jets. He got New York on the board with a 13-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter and rounded out the scoring in the fourth with a 12-yard touchdown reception and the ensuing two-point conversion. The 2025 second-round pick entered Sunday's action with just one touchdown in 17 career regular-season appearances, but Taylor posted the best performance of his young career while outplaying 2026 first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq, who had just one catch for six yards. Taylor will continue to face competition for targets from Sadiq, as well as the wide-receiver trio of Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper and Adonai Mitchell, in Week 8 against the Raiders.

short_comment: Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins. He also rushed twice for no gain and threw a successful two-point conversion.
long_comment: Smith matched Miami's opening-drive touchdown with a 13-yard touchdown pass to Mason Taylor on the Jets' first drive, but the veteran QB threw an interception deep in Dolphins territory on the next drive. The Jets trailed for the entirety of the last three quarters, allowing Smith to rack up some big numbers during their failed comeback bid, as he posted his second three-touchdown performance of the season. He found Omar Cooper for a three-yard touchdown in the third quarter after they connected for a 60-yard gain earlier on that drive, and Smith threw a 12-yard touchdown and two-point conversion, both to Taylor, to round out the scoring with 3:24 remaining in the fourth. However, the Dolphins ran out the clock from there to drop the Jets to 2-5 heading into a Week 8 home game against the Raiders.

short_comment: Wilson caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
long_comment: Wilson wasn't targeted in the first half as the Jets took a 21-7 deficit into the locker room. He was slightly more involved in the second half, but Wilson was overshadowed for a second consecutive game by rookie first-round pick Omar Cooper, who has exceeded 100 receiving yards with a touchdown in both games since recovering from an ankle injury. Wilson will try to bounce back from this season-worst performance in catches, receiving yards and targets when the Jets host the Raiders in Week 8.

short_comment: Cooper caught all five of his targets for 115 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
long_comment: Cooper topped 100 receiving yards with a TD for the second time in as many games since returning from an ankle injury sustained in his regular-season debut. The rookie 30th overall pick had a 52-yard catch in the first quarter and a 60-yard catch in the third, then added a three-yard touchdown reception three plays after the second long catch. Cooper has been a big-play machine when healthy, and he'll look to build on his strong start in Week 8 against the Raiders.

short_comment: Allen rushed 17 times for 104 yards and caught six of seven targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
long_comment: Allen worked as the lead back for a fourth consecutive game, as Breece Hall (quadriceps) was ultimately inactive after being listed as questionable heading into the game. The 235-pound Allen continued to struggle in short yardage, getting stuffed on a goal-line attempt in the fourth quarter as the Jets were denied a game-tying touchdown and instead settled for a field goal to cut the deficit to four points with 8:57 remaining. Allen has exceeded 100 rushing yards twice during Hall's absence but has just one touchdown over that span and two touchdowns this season. Hall worked ahead of Allen prior to getting hurt, but they may split the backfield workload more evenly if Hall's cleared to return against the Raiders in Week 8.

short_comment: Sweat (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Sweat exited during the third quarter with a knee injury. The starting defensive tackle will likely be replaced by a rotation of Darrell Jackson and Jowon Briggs.

short_comment: The Jets placed Mauigoa (quadriceps) on injured reserve Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Mauigoa suited up for the Jets' Week 6 loss to the Patriots before being ruled out for Week 7 against the Browns. The linebacker has missed three regular-season games so far in 2026 and will need to miss at least four more while on IR.

short_comment: DeJean recorded seven tackles (three solo) during Monday's 38-21 loss versus the Cowboys.
long_comment: DeJean racked up seven-plus tackles for the third time this season in a Week 7 contest that saw Dallas run the ball 38 times. He's on pace for the first 100-tackle season of his career, putting him on the fringe of IDP consideration of some formats ahead of a Week 8 matchup at Washington.

short_comment: Baun recorded nine tackles (two solo) and a pass defensed during Monday's 38-21 loss versus the Cowboys.
long_comment: Dallas' offense found a ton of success on the ground in Week 7, and its 38 rush attempts created plenty of tackling opportunities for Baun. He now has nine-plus tackles in four of his six games in 2026. He figures as a high-floor IDP option in some formats heading into a Week 8 tilt at Washington.

short_comment: Moore caught both of his targets for 16 yards during Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys.
long_comment: Moore had the opportunity to work in an expanded role Monday due to the absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Moore's 22 snaps on offense were fourth-most among Eagles wide receivers and he logged season highs in both catches and receiving yards. However, the Eagles' offense as a whole struggled without its top wide receivers, and Moore would revert to a deep rotational role against the Commanders on Sunday if one or both of Smith and Wicks were cleared to return.

short_comment: Stowers failed to haul in his lone target during Monday's 38-21 loss to Dallas.
long_comment: The rookie second-rounder was activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday's contest after missing the first six games of the regular season due to quad and hamstring injuries that he picked up during training camp. He played a total of 21 snaps (12 on offense, nine on special teams) in his NFL debut, but his lone target from Tanner McKee came within the last two minutes of the fourth quarter, when the game was well out of reach for Philadelphia. Stowers will likely be limited to TE3 duties behind Dallas Goedert and Johnny Mundt for the time being.

short_comment: Cooper caught one of three passes for 17 yards during the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday.
long_comment: With both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) sidelined, the Eagles' wide receiver group was led by Cooper, rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown during Monday's contest. Cooper led the position group with 61 offensive snaps, but he only had a 17-yard catch to show for it, which he logged on the Eagles' final play of the first quarter. He has only two catches on five targets for 26 yards over his last two games, and his profile as a boom-or-bust touchdown option in fantasy is severely hampered with Tanner McKee under center instead of Jalen Hurts (calf, IR). The Eagles will hit the road for Week 8 against the Commanders on Sunday.

short_comment: Barkley said after Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys that his "hamstring came out great," and noted that the back issue that kept him out for the entire fourth quarter isn't anything that he expects to prevent him from playing Sunday against the Commanders, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: While suiting up for the first time since Week 4 after missing the Eagles' previous two games due to a hamstring strain, Barkley took the field for just 10 snaps on the night but was impactful in his limited playing time. He touched the ball on nine of those snaps, carrying seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown to go with two receptions for nine yards on two targets. Heading into the game, the Eagles had deliberately planned to manage Barkley's workload to some extent, but he ended up seeing fewer snaps than anticipated after his back locked up on him following a 29-yard run in the first quarter. He didn't end up taking any snaps after the third quarter, with the Eagles leaning exclusively on Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) and Elijah Mitchell out of the backfield over the final 15 minutes. Fortunately for Barkley, the back issue doesn't seem to be a major concern, but his activity in practice this week will warrant monitoring as the Eagles assess his availability for Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Pierce didn't take the field for either of the Eagles' final two possessions of Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys after sustaining an undisclosed injury with 8:38 remaining in the fourth quarter, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
long_comment: Pierce was the second Eagles running back to make an early exit from Monday's contest, as starter Saquon Barkley was held out for the entire fourth quarter while nursing hamstring and back injuries. Before leaving the contest, Pierce carried 14 times for 47 yards and a touchdown while adding a one-yard reception on his lone target. Ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Commanders, the Eagles will issue their next injury report Wednesday, when the nature of Pierce's health concern as well as the extent of his practice activity will be revealed.

long_comment: Brown saw an expanded role due to the absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), and the veteran wideout finished third in receiving yards and targets as a result. Brown's stats were his first of the season, and although there have been some rumblings about him being a potential trade candidate, the Eagles' lack of healthy bodies at the position could give Brown some job security through the deadline.

short_comment: Goedert secured five of seven targets for 48 yards in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
long_comment: On a night when both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were sidelined, Goedert served as an even more important target than usual. The veteran tight end finished second in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Eagles on the night, and he's now recorded at least five catches in three consecutive games. Goedert has 24 targets over that span as well, and he should remain similarly busy in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night.

short_comment: Lemon brought in seven of eight targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
long_comment: Lemon operated as the Eagles' de facto No. 1 receiver on a night where both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were sidelined, and the rookie met the moment by posting career- and team-high figures across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Lemon rounded out his solid performance by recording his first NFL touchdown catch on a four-yard scoring grab with just under six minutes remaining in the third quarter. Lemon could have another opportunity to spearhead the air attack in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night, as both Smith and Wicks may be hard-pressed to get healthy enough to suit up for that contest.

short_comment: McKee completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception and added one rush for one yard in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
long_comment: McKee's final numbers weren't poor by any stretch, but the fourth-year signal-caller couldn't come close to keeping pace with Dak Prescott's exploits. McKee was working without both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), so in that context, the quarterback's production was solid, albeit unspectacular. McKee recorded completions to eight different targets overall, and he'll look to boost his overall numbers with a hopefully healthier receiving corps in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night.

short_comment: Covey (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday's contest versus the Cowboys.
long_comment: Covey appeared to injure his knee during the opening kickoff Monday, and Philadelphia will now have to finish the game without him. All of his snaps so far this season have come on special teams, and Elijah Moore and Dameon Pierce are the next men up in the return game for the Eagles.

short_comment: Bennett (knee) will remain on injured reserve and is inactive for Monday night's matchup with Dallas.
long_comment: Bennett isn't quite ready to come off of IR after returning to practice Oct. 14. The cornerback is still working his way back from a knee injury that he suffered in late August, and his next chance to return to action will come in Week 8 versus the Commanders.

short_comment: Dickerson (knee) was activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday night's matchup with the Cowboys.
long_comment: Dickerson is all set to return to action after missing the team's last five games while recovering from a knee injury that he suffered in Week 1. The 28-year-old will be back in his starting role at left guard versus Dallas.

short_comment: Hunt (ankle/knee) is available for Monday's game versus Dallas.
long_comment: Hunt has been battling a few injuries. He didn't play in the Week 6 loss to Carolina, though he will return against the Cowboys. With Jonathan Greenard (ankle) also available, Hunt could see fewer snaps.

short_comment: Greenard (ankle) is available for Monday's game against the Cowboys.
long_comment: Greenard has been battling an ankle injury. He was considered a game-time decision, though he will be active for the second consecutive contest.

short_comment: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive for Monday's game against the Cowboys but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback.
long_comment: Payton will serve as the emergency signal-caller, meaning he won't be able to play unless Tanner McKee and Joe Milton exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

long_comment: Mitchell figures to operate as the RB3 behind Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Dameon Pierce. Mitchell has appeared in just one regular-season game since the 2023 season.

short_comment: The Eagles activated Calcaterra (back) from injured reserve Monday.
long_comment: Calcaterra has been cleared to play Monday night against Dallas, giving Philly another capable tight end behind Dallas Goedert. It's unclear how the playing time will shake out between blocker Johnny Mundt, catch-first rookie Eli Stowers and Calcaterra, but the Eagles could lean into the tight end-heavy sets with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) both ruled out.

short_comment: Wilson totaled six tackles (three solo) and an interception during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.
long_comment: Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.

short_comment: Queen compiled 10 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.
long_comment: Queen had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles in addition to registering his first sack of the campaign. The 2020 first-round pick has now logged 48 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across seven games this season.

short_comment: Bernard caught three of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
long_comment: It was a big step back in production for the rookie wideout compared to Week 6 against the Bucs, but Bernard still ran a team-high 33 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 34 dropbacks against New Orleans. Bernard's role is secure while Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) remain sidelined for at least two more games each. Bernard will be a fantasy WR3 for next Sunday's game against the Browns.

short_comment: Smith reverted to the Steelers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
long_comment: Smith caught both his targets for 24 yards in Sunday's win over the Saints in Paris. The wide receiver played 29 offensive snaps in the contest, good for 45 percent of the team's total offensive plays. Smith has no practice-squad elevations remaining, meaning he will need to sign with the Steelers' 53-man roster to suit up again for Pittsburgh this season.

short_comment: Washington caught his lone target for a four-yard touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints in Paris.
long_comment: Washington made his one catch count, out-muscling a defender for the goal-line score. The burly tight end has Aaron Rodgers' eyes in the scoring area and now has a touchdown in back-to-back weeks and three of his last four outings. On the year, Washington has 16 grabs for 160 yards and three scores on 23 targets. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet most weeks.

short_comment: Freiermuth caught two of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
long_comment: Over the last two weeks, Freiermuth has just four grabs for 31 yards on seven targets. In that same span, Darnell Washington has secured five grabs for 29 yards and two touchdowns as one of Aaron Rodgers' preferred targets in the red zone. Freiermuth is in the large bucket of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.

short_comment: Boswell made each of his three field-goal attempts and his lone extra-point try in a 16-10 victory over the Saints on Sunday in Paris.
long_comment: Boswell opened Sunday's contest with a 28-yard chip shot early in the first quarter before connecting on field goals from 47 and 39 yards in the second and third, respectively. It's the third time this season that he has made at least three field goals, and through seven regular-season games, he is 16-for-20 on field-goal attempts (including 4-for-6 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 13-for-13 on extra-point tries. The Steelers will return home for a Week 8, AFC North showdown against the Browns on Nov. 1.

short_comment: Metcalf two of six targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
long_comment: The Steelers' offense mostly flowed through its backfield, and Metcalf's 56 receiving yards actually led the team despite the fact that his two catches were a season low. The veteran wideout's target volume has been erratic this year, but he remains Aaron Rodgers' top downfield option. Metcalf will take a 32-374-1 line on 58 targets through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Browns, who he produced a 5-115-0 line against in Week 4.

short_comment: Dowdle carried the ball nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: The 15 touches were a season high for Dowdle, but he still took a back seat to Jaylen Warren's 21 touches and 137 scrimmage yards in the Steelers' backfield. Dowdle also led the team in receptions on the day, and his own 86 combined yards were a season high. Pittsburgh could stay with its ground-heavy game plan in Week 8 against Cleveland, giving Dowdle some fantasy appeal even in his backup role.

short_comment: Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 passes and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints. He added six yards on three carries.
long_comment: The Steelers' offense relied heavily on its backfield in this one, as Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for 36 touches and 223 scrimmage yards. Rodgers did produce the team's only TD of the day on a four-yard toss to Darnell Washington in the second quarter. The veteran QB will take a 13:5 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Browns, who Rodgers threw three touchdowns and a season-high 299 yards against in Week 4.

short_comment: Warren carried the ball 18 times for 101 yards and caught three of four targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
long_comment: The 21 touches tied his season high, while Rico Dowdle got 15 as the Steelers went with a ground-heavy game plan. Warren has topped 100 scrimmage yards in four of the last five games, racking up 472 rushing yards and a TD along with a 17-233-1 line on 24 targets during that hot stretch. He'll remain one of the key pieces of the Pittsburgh offense heading into a Week 8 clash at home against a Cleveland defense that Warren recorded 126 combined yards against in Week 4.

short_comment: Elliott (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris.
long_comment: Elliott will suit up for his first game action since Oct. 26, 2025, when he sustained a knee injury that kept him out for the remainder of that season as well as the first six games of the 2026 campaign. The 29-year-old was a full participant in practice this week, and after being activated from injured reserve Saturday, he'll likely be ready to handle a full load of snaps against New Orleans. Expect Elliott to unseat rookie Robert Spears-Jennings as one of Pittsburgh's starting safeties.

short_comment: Rudolph is active for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
long_comment: Rudolph has emerged as the Steelers' preferred backup quarterback behind starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers coming out of the preseason. Through each of Pittsburgh's first seven contests, Rudolph has suited up, while both Will Howard and Drew Allar have been inactive. Howard is the Steelers' emergency No. 3 quarterback and will be called upon to play only in the event that both Rodgers and Rudolph are forced to exit Sunday's game.

short_comment: Watt (calf) practiced fully Friday and doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Saints.
long_comment: Watt was limited by a calf injury Thursday, but he's good to go for Pittsburgh's Paris game against New Orleans. Through six games this season, the 32-year-old Watt has 15 tackles (10 solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and a pick-six interception.

short_comment: Joseph-Day (triceps) was placed on injured reserve by the Steelers on Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official website reports.
long_comment: Joseph-Day is dealing with an apparent triceps injury, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Gabriel Rubio and Kevin Jobity are both candidates to see an increase in workload on Pittsburgh's defensive line.

short_comment: Brisker posted seven tackles (four solo) during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
long_comment: Brisker played every single defensive snap for the fifth time in six games this season, and he has logged at least six tackles in each of those outings. He's up to 41 combined tackles in 2026 and is on track to crack 100 tackles for the third time in his NFL career and the first time since 2023, when he played for the Bears.

short_comment: Herbig recorded six solo tackles, including 2.0 sacks, during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
long_comment: Herbig did not record a sack through the first five games of the regular season, but the fourth-year pro got to quarterback Jalon Daniels twice during Sunday's OT victory. Herbig is up to 18 tackles (13 solo) and one forced fumble through six regular-season games while working in a rotational role on defense.

short_comment: Greenlaw posted 12 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's loss to the Falcons.
long_comment: Greenlaw missed Week 6 against Washington while on suspension but returned Sunday and logged a season-high 91 percent defensive snap share. The veteran linebacker tied his season high with 12 tackles, finishing one behind Fred Warner for the team lead. Greenlaw is enjoying a productive return to San Francisco with 49 tackles and a forced fumble through six contests.

short_comment: Warner recorded 13 tackles (six solo) Sunday in a Week 7 loss to Atlanta.
long_comment: Warner led the 49ers in tackles, finishing one ahead of Dre Greenlaw. It was the fourth time through seven games that Warner has notched double-digit stops. The star linebacker ranks second in the NFL with 71 tackles through seven games.
